articleTitle: LCC Matching Network Design for a MHz Class D GaN PA Considering Parameter Uncertainties
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Power Technology Conference and Expo (WPTCE)
abstract: The LCC matching network plays an important part in Megahertz Wireless Power Transfer (MHz WPT) systems. The soft switching technique is another topic that needs to be focused on when designing MHz WPT systems. In this paper, the impedance converting characteristics of the LCC matching network is applied to realize the soft switching of Megahertz Class D GaN power amplifiers (MHz Class D GaN PA). The criterion for the soft switching of MHz Class D GaN PA is expressed in the form of a simple equation. Parameter uncertainties in real MHz WPT systems are unavoidable and corresponding analysis is also conducted. A 6.78 MHz WPT system with Class D PA is built to realize robust soft switching and to measure the output capacitor of GaN components. The results show that the expected robust soft switching is realized when the output power changes.

articleTitle: High-Performance Multi-MHz Dynamic Capacitive Wireless Power Transfer System Using Asymmetric Couplers
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Power Technology Conference and Expo (WPTCE)
abstract: The paper presents a high-power density multi-MHz dynamic capacitive wireless power transfer (WPT) system for wireless charging of mobile robots that leverages asymmetric couplers to achieve an improved misalignment tolerance. A methodology to design such couplers is presented. Furthermore, the impact of varying the physical parameters of the proposed asymmetric couplers is studied. Two 6.78-MHz 3-cm air-gap 2-kW capacitive WPT prototypes (one using conventional couplers and the other using the proposed asymmetric couplers) are designed and built to validate the proposed methodology. The developed prototype leveraging asymmetric couplers exhibit a significant improvement in misalignment tolerance i.e., 100% nominal output power delivery at ± 50% misalignment, with 85% peak experimental efficiency, as compared to the conventional prototype that can only deliver 35% nominal output power at ± 50% misalignment. Moreover, the proposed use of asymmetric couplers on the secondary-side offers a simple, efficient, and cost-effective alternative to active compensation techniques.

articleTitle: High Power Electric Generation and WPT Demonstration Mission
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Power Technology Conference and Expo (WPTCE)
abstract: Space Solar Power is becoming one of the important development directions for the world to tackle the climate change. High power generation and long distance wireless power transmission are the most important technologies of SSP and need to be demonstrated step by step to meet the demand to construct the commercial SSP. This paper presents a proposed first-step demonstration mission in space. The mission includes a main spacecraft and an energy receiving spacecraft in LEO. The main spacecraft will emit about 4kW microwave and 1km laser to the receiving station on ground to demonstration the WPT chain. At same time, the receiving spacecraft will receive laser to demonstrate LPT in space.

articleTitle: Design of the coupling coils with misalignment tolerance for underwater charging applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Power Technology Conference and Expo (WPTCE)
abstract: This paper focuses on the research and the design of coupling coils of an underwater wireless charging station system. The system must adapt to the underwater environment and address alignment issues caused by seawater as the medium. A detailed investigation of coil coupling design is conducted, considering the unique underwater dynamic environment. An automated coil evaluation platform is established by integrating COMSOL Multiphysics® and Matlab software. The Exhaustive Search Method is used to optimize the coil inner radius design to achieve high misalignment tolerance. Finally, the optimized coils are applied in a H-bridge series-series resonant converter and compared to a control group of coils. The optimized coils show superior misalignment tolerance, with minimal coupling coefficient variation (i.e. 0.013) and an average coupling level of 0.232. In contrast, the control group exhibits a higher coupling coefficient variation (i.e. 0.026) and an average coupling level of 0.18 under the same conditions.

articleTitle: Photodynamic Therapy with Wireless Power Transfer for Deep Organ Cancer Application
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Power Technology Conference and Expo (WPTCE)
abstract: Recently, photodynamic therapy (PDT) has been attracting attention as a new treatment method with fewer side effects than conventional cancer treatment methods. However, PDT is currently applicable only to those cancer types that can be directly irradiated by wired light. In this paper, we designed a compact power receiving device and a wireless power transfer (WPT) system containing an LED with an emission wavelength of 660 nm for long-term implantation in the body. Then, experiments were conducted to induce cancer cell death by photodynamic therapy using WPT light irradiation and a porphyrin derivative that exhibits nuclear transfer. As a result, 94% of the cells were successfully induced to die after 60 minutes of light irradiation.

articleTitle: A Compact High-Efficiency Wideband Watt-Level RF Rectifier for Microwave Power Transfer
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Power Technology Conference and Expo (WPTCE)
abstract: In this paper, a novel compact high-efficiency wideband watt-level RF rectifier is proposed for Microwave Power Transfer (MPT). Compared with the typical Schottky Barrier Diode (SBD) rectifier circuit, the input power level of the proposed rectifier is significantly improved without reducing rectification efficiency by utilizing integrated SBDs arrays. An LCC impedance matching network is proposed to cascade in the front end of a voltage-doubling rectification topology for increasing the bandwidth and doubling the power capacity of the rectifier. For validation, a rectifier with the center operating frequency at 433 MHz has been designed and fabricated. The measurement results shown that, the RF-dc conversion efficiency is higher than 76% with the input power at 30 dBm in the band between 383 MHz and 483 MHz. Moreover, the overall size of the rectifier circuit is only 3 cm × 3 cm (0.043 λ0 × 0.043 λ0). Therefore, the proposed compact wideband rectifier is suitable for watt-level power output MPT systems applications.

articleTitle: A Novel Approach for Mutual Inductance Estimation in Wireless Power Transfer
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Power Technology Conference and Expo (WPTCE)
abstract: In this work, a mutual inductance estimation (MIE) method for multiple transmitters (multi-Txs) wireless charging systems is proposed. The method involves intermittently interrupting the power to the transmitter, while simultaneously collecting current data, to estimate the mutual inductance parameters. The estimation process does not involve high-order calculations, making it simple to compute. The proposed method eliminates the need for continuous high-speed real-time feedback signals from the receiver (Rx) to adjust current or voltage. Hence, it avoids the interference issues of high-order switching harmonics between power converters and the wireless communication link. This enhances the reliability and reduces the cost of the wireless communication module. The simulation results prove that the proposed method can accurately estimate mutual inductance under various coupling conditions, with errors consistently below 3.5%.

articleTitle: Assessing Preferences for Dynamic Wireless Power Transfer in Public Charging Choices Among Experienced and non-Experienced EV Users
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Power Technology Conference and Expo (WPTCE)
abstract: This paper explores preference for dynamic wireless power transfer (DWPT) technology in public charging choices. DWPT can alleviate range anxiety and charging time as barriers to electric vehicle (EV) use. Using the case of Indiana, this study designed a stated choice (SC) experiment, presenting respondents with various scenarios for extended electric vehicle (EV) trips. Integrated choice latent variable (ICLV) model was estimated to determine the factors influencing public charging decisions, particularly from the perspectives of experienced and non-experienced EV users. In general, DWPT is a more suitable option for experience users, however, the result remains inconclusive due to insignificant estimation. Conversely, nonexperienced users exhibit a negative perception towards DWPT relative to Level 2 charging. Moreover, experienced users are more sensitive to charging cost which make it necessary to make sure DWPT charging fee is competitive among other options. The non-experienced female also finds DWPT an unsuitable option, which corresponds to the charging preference distribution where DWPT is the least chosen option. Recognizing these nuanced preferences can assist policymakers in formulating targeted strategies to optimize public charging utilization and attract a broader spectrum of EV adopters, with DWPT emerging as a central focus in this endeavor.

articleTitle: Design of Wireless Power Transfer Cage for Uniform Magnetic Field to Implantable Medical Devices Mounted on Animals
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Power Technology Conference and Expo (WPTCE)
abstract: Many studies are conducted to apply wireless power transfer (WPT) technology to ensure non-invasiveness and minimize maintenance of implantable medical devices (IMDs). Commercialization of medical devices involves animal testing. During animal testing, misalignment between the transmitter and receiver can occur due to the animal's free movement, which lead to a decrease in power transfer capacity and efficiency, or even to a disruption in power transfer. Therefore, this paper proposes a cage-type WPT coil design method to deliver uniform power to a receiver coil whose position changes. The proposed method divides one transmitter coil into several zones and creates a uniform magnetic field by varying the design for each zone. By adjusting the current direction, the magnetic field within the transmitter coil can be shaped, and the number of turns and the spacing between sections can be designed to improve the performance of the WPT system. It can be confirmed that the proposed method is capable of forming a uniform magnetic field and delivering uniform power through 3D EM simulation and circuit simulation.

articleTitle: Interleaved Boost Converter Integrated Inductive Power Transfer System for Wireless Vehicle Charging Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Power Technology Conference and Expo (WPTCE)
abstract: The proposed onboard wireless charger is new with respect to the kind of onboard AC/ DC topologies used with the receiver unit. It is based on the cascade connection of two-phase interleaved boost converter and full bridge resonant circuit. It offers wide range control of voltage gain and also bears higher efficiency due to single stage power conversion for the received power. Due to superior efficiency, constant current operation and high performance under misalignment conditions double sided LCC compensation has been used for the resonant tank. This topology also saves number of active switch count by sharing of switches between the two-phase boost converter and full bridge resonant circuit. Also, there is no need of isolation of receiver coil during the discharging of the EV battery due to use of LCC compensation. The proposed charger topology is simulated using MATLAB simulation platform to validate the charge/ discharge operation of the wireless charger and also a scale down prototype is built to verify these functionality.

articleTitle: Passive Microwave Sensors Based on Quasi-BIC
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Power Technology Conference and Expo (WPTCE)
abstract: With the rapid development of automated systems, it became necessary to use wireless communication systems to monitor a variety of different parameters. Wireless sensors are actively used in many modern intelligent systems to track and control various characteristics of the system and its environment. The task of developing compact sensors with high sensitivity and measurement accuracy is extremely urgent in this field. In this paper, two microwave sensor designs based on dielectric resonators, whose parameters are optimized for quasi-BIC mode maintenance, have been proposed. Furthermore, the application of these sensors extends to the realm of temperature tracking, water temperature control, and impurity detection, showcasing their potential in manufacturing processes, wireless power transfer, and various other industrial applications.

articleTitle: Two-Stage Passive Impedance Matching Network With Frequency Modulation Strategy
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Power Technology Conference and Expo (WPTCE)
abstract: The mismatched impedance for PA caused by coil misalignment or load change, affects the efficiency of the wireless power transfer (WPT) system. In this paper, based on the narrowband frequency modulation, a two-stage passive matching network is proposed, which can match the varying load to the characteristic impedance of the PA. The limitation of a single T-network in frequency modulation is analyzed while the reactance nulling network and resistance conversion network are introduced. The detailed design method and frequency selection strategy are presented. To verify the feasibility of the network, the example matching network is designed for inductive loads, and a 1000W prototype is built with a reflected coefficient of less than 0.2.

articleTitle: Computational Study of Transmitting Phased Array Antennas for WPT Demonstration Satellite Experiment
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Power Technology Conference and Expo (WPTCE)
abstract: The purpose of this study is investigation of transmitting phased array antennas for a future wireless power transfer (WPT) demonstration satellite experiment. A sequential array was used to construct an array antenna to improve the overall axial ratio of the transmitting array antenna. We evaluate the characteristics based on simulations for three types of arrays. We conduct experiments using the model determined in the simulations to validate the reliability of the simulations.

articleTitle: WPT using High Frequency Rotary Transformer for Separately Excited Synchronous Generator
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Power Technology Conference and Expo (WPTCE)
abstract: This paper proposes a novel high frequency rotary transformer (HFRT) structure for a separately excited synchronous generator (SESG) used in offshore wind turbines. The SESG can eliminate and reduce rare earth permanent magnet (REPM) usage and provide a better performance in offshore wind turbine systems. However, the major drawback of such SESG is the necessity of brushes and slip rings to supply the field current, which increases the maintenance cost and operation reliability. To overcome these problems, an HFRT integrated with SiC Schottky diodes can be used to replace brushes and slip rings in the SESG. In contrast to conventional low-frequency rotary transformers, the HFRT working at over 100kHz operating frequency exhibits excellent performance of Wireless Power Transfer (WPT) efficiency and significant size reduction. The proposed HFRT features a high frequency magnetic ferrite for both the stationary part as the transformer primary and the rotating part as the transformer secondary and a large air gap, allowing safe operation at high rotational speeds. Hence, this novel rotary transformer can enable the adoption of a wound rotor synchronous generator.

articleTitle: Research on Improving Wireless Power Transmission Efficiency by Forming a Flat-Topped Beam Using Simple Phased Array
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Power Technology Conference and Expo (WPTCE)
abstract: In this study, simple phased arrays used as a power transmitting antenna in near-field wireless power transmission at 28 GHz band were investigated by electromagnetic field simulations. In particular, beamforming using a flat-topped beam was carried out to improve the power transmission efficiency. The change in transmission efficiency when the number of receiving antenna elements is varied was calculated using simulation results. The calculation results show that threshold qualified arrays can provide efficiencies close to those of fully driven arrays, regardless of the number of receiving antenna elements.

articleTitle: Boosting RF-DC Rectification via Bias Voltage
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Power Technology Conference and Expo (WPTCE)
abstract: This letter explores the potential benefits of incorporating a bias voltage in the operation of an RF rectifier diode. Despite the challenges posed by network matching and additional power consumption, the study demonstrates efficiency enhancements across a range of input power levels. These enhancements offer significant advantages for active energy harvesters equipped with a controllable small bias source.

articleTitle: Low-Order Harmonic Mitigation for Inductive Wireless Power Transfer Using a Three-Phase Meander Coil Topology
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Power Technology Conference and Expo (WPTCE)
abstract: An improvement in the polyphase system for Wireless Power Transfer (WPT) is presented in this article to reduce the impact of the low-order harmonics in the air gap and on the induced voltage at the receiver pad. The proposed solution is studied using a simplified analytical model, and later, a more complex topology is introduced and analysed using a Finite Element Method software. The results show that it is possible to mitigate the fifth, seventh and eleventh harmonic without a significant increment in the air gap between the WPT pads. Furthermore, a dynamic model for a balanced system with a three-phase transmitter and multiple phases with a series of resonant tanks on the receiver side is developed using four states instead of eight.

articleTitle: A Self-Resonant Litz-Based Cable for Inductive Power Transfer
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Power Technology Conference and Expo (WPTCE)
abstract: This paper presents a new cable design that offers embedded capacitance. This is useful in the design of coils for wirelessly charging electric vehicles at 85kHz since it enables the elimination of compensation circuits. This paper presents the methodology and results of extensive computer modelling of this innovative cable for coil design applications and compares them to equivalent models using conventional Litz wire in a comparison of impedances.

articleTitle: Decomposition and Compromise of Microwave Power Beam Steering Error
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Power Technology Conference and Expo (WPTCE)
abstract: Retro-directive microwave power transmission helps to guarantee the beam collection efficiency for dynamic application systems. To regulate the power steering error, it was decomposed into several factors and items. Then compromise was done among them. The direction of arrival estimation and beam steering experiment was conducted and the measured results were analyzed.

articleTitle: Millimeter-Wave 5G Relay Transceivers Using Wireless Power Transfer and Backscatter
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Power Technology Conference and Expo (WPTCE)
abstract: This paper introduces wirelessly-powered millimeter-wave 5G relay transceivers. The proposed relay transceivers enable wireless communication at 28GHz leveraging the 24GHz wireless power transfer signal. The relay transceiver realizes beamforming and frequency conversion with drastically lower power consumption, which can be supplied by the WPT generation power. This paper briefly introduces the fabricated prototypes of the wirelessly powered relay transceivers.

articleTitle: Maximizing Energy Efficiency for Wireless Power Transfer Systems Through an Optimal Frequency Control Strategy
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Power Technology Conference and Expo (WPTCE)
abstract: This paper proposes a novel optimal frequency control strategy to maximize the wireless power transfer (WPT) energy efficiency across a wide load range and coupling conditions. The proposed approach focuses on achieving the optimal frequency over the feasible frequency range by meeting the optimal resistive and reactive equivalent load conditions simultaneously. The effectiveness of the method is demonstrated through a 48W simulated WPT system. The performance of the proposed control method is evaluated for load variations from 20% to 100% and coupling coefficient variations from 0.1 to 0.3. Comparative analysis with the state-of-the-art control method shows significant improvements in terms of efficiency under different operating conditions.

articleTitle: All-Polarized Wideband Rectenna Array for Omnidirectional Wireless Energy Harvesting
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Power Technology Conference and Expo (WPTCE)
abstract: In this work, a 3-D omnidirectional multiple polarized radio-frequency (RF) energy harvester (rectenna) array with broadband frequency coverages (2.4–3.1 GHz) is presented. The rectenna array strategically combines 12 single microstrip slot antenna elements placed in a transparent octahedral box. A broadband microstrip slot antenna based on multiple resonant stubs is proposed and studied. By utilizing two pairs of stubs embedded on a defective ground, a reflection coefficient of less than −10 dB can be achieved with broadband characteristics for applications of wireless local area network (WLAN). A broadband rectifier array is designed with 12 rectifier elements arranged in a 360-degree array. All elements are connected in parallel to achieve maximum DC combining and reduce losses caused by feed lines during array formation. The RF-DC conversation efficiency of the rectifier array is 75 % at an input power of 13 dBm. The experimental results show that this rectenna array works well with RF radiations at either horizontal or vertical polarization from various directions.

articleTitle: Development of Air-Core Beamforming Antenna With 24 GHz Band 25 W Class Power Feed Circuit
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Power Technology Conference and Expo (WPTCE)
abstract: In this study, we have developed a radial line-slot antenna that forms an air-core beam suitable for wireless power transmission. By using the Laguerre-Gaussian mode (OAM-mode), air-core beam can be formed in which the center intensity is null. This feature is useful to avoid interference with equipment placed in the center of the receiving antenna. The desired aperture plane distribution was obtained from the analytical solution of the beam, and the slot antenna pair that realizes the aperture plane distribution was designed. Four coaxial probes with excitation phases differing by 90 degrees each were used to excite m=3 rotational modes in the radial waveguide. The diameter of the designed 24-GHz RLSA was 300 mm, and the total output power of the developed 4-port feeding circuit was 25 W. Using these devices, we plan to conduct proof of concept for wireless power transmission to drone.

articleTitle: A High-Dynamic Range 5.8 GHz Band 1 W Rectifier MMIC With Low Threshold Voltage GaAs GADs
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Power Technology Conference and Expo (WPTCE)
abstract: In this paper, the 5.8 GHz band 1 W rectifier with low threshold voltage GaAs gated anode diodes (GADs) is demonstrated for extension to low power operation. The GaAs GAD has an advantage of controllability on threshold voltage. This enables low threshold voltage of GaAs GAD that is similar value as a Si SBD. In the developed 5.8 GHz band 1 W rectifier, measured rectification efficiency of 77 % at input power of 30 dBm is obtained. At input power of 10 dBm, efficiency is 56 % that is extreme higher value than those of 1 W class rectifiers. It is clarified that low threshold voltage GaAs GAD is effective for rectification in high dynamic range.

articleTitle: Selective Activation of Transmitter Coils to Reduce Leakage Magnetic Fields in Wireless Power Transfer Systems with Multiple Transmitters
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Power Technology Conference and Expo (WPTCE)
abstract: In wireless power transfer systems, the leakage magnetic field must be kept below a certain specified value, as it can affect the human body or electronic devices in the vicinity. Consequently, many studies have been conducted to reduce the leakage magnetic fields in wireless power transfer systems. This paper aims to minimize the generation of unnecessary magnetic fields by arranging multiple transmitter coils and activating only specific transmitter coils that correspond to the position or size of the receiver coil. It analyzes the magnitude of the current depending on the number of activated transmitter coils and the resulting size of the leakage magnetic field, and discusses a method for selecting transmitter coils to minimize the leakage magnetic field. The proposed method has been verified to reduce the magnetic field by about 53% in a 300 W class WPT system compared to using a single TX.

articleTitle: Conductive and Capacitive Properties of Couplers under Seawater for Electric Wireless Power Transfer
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Power Technology Conference and Expo (WPTCE)
abstract: This paper analyzes the modeling and characteristics of parallel-plate capacitors for underwater capacitive wireless power transfer (CWPT) systems. Using finite element method (FEM) simulations, this paper investigates the impact of various simulation factors on the simulation results both for the capacitances and the conductances. A fitting equation is proposed for the coupling capacitance and conductance in seawater environment, which matches the simulation results well. Notably, this paper firstly demonstrates a ratio of around 295.9 at a frequency of 3 MHz between the real and imaginary parts of the coupling admittance. This result confirms that the conductance, rather than the susceptance, dominates the CWPT system for under seawater applications.

articleTitle: Effect of Antenna Position Deviation of Large-scale Phased Array and its Compensation via Retro-reflective Beamforming for SSPS
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Power Technology Conference and Expo (WPTCE)
abstract: The effect of antenna position deviations on the beamforming performance of large-scale phased arrays are modeled and simulated for microwave power transmission (MPT). Near-field effects are included in the modeling, so that accurate simulation results can be obtained in the application scenarios of space solar power station (SSPS). Method of calculating field distribution of the microwave power beam over the receiving aperture with typical deformation of the transmitting aperture as well as random position deviation of the antenna modules is developed. Based on the method, numerical results are provided to demonstrate the retro-reflective beamforming performance in compensating the effect of antenna position deviations in a typical SSPS MPT system.

articleTitle: Diode Selection Strategies of RF Power Harvester to Improve Temperature Resilience of Battery-free Wireless Sensing
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Power Technology Conference and Expo (WPTCE)
abstract: Temperature changes may lead to performance degradation or operation interruption in practical wireless sensing applications. Thus, the capability of an RF power harvester to provide stable and reliable dc output under temperature changes is critical for the proper operation of battery-free wireless sensing. This work presents a system analysis of a multi-stage RF power harvester considering a voltage comparator for wireless sensing as its load. Both theoretical and measurement results reveal that a Schottky diode with a higher nonlinear junction resistance is preferred, as it reduces mismatch loss and allows more harvested dc power to be delivered to its load. This work shows that the SMS7621 diode-based 3-stage harvester can provide stable 3.3-V dc output over a wide temperature range of −40 ºC to 80 ºC, which can significantly improve the temperature resilience of battery-free wireless sensing.

articleTitle: On-Body Flexible Energy Harvesting Antenna Design Aided by Characteristic Mode Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Power Technology Conference and Expo (WPTCE)
abstract: This paper introduces an on-body, flexible energy-harvesting antenna, utilizing characteristic mode analysis (CMA) to enhance and predict its design and performance under bending conditions. The initial design features a simple E-shaped patch antenna, with structural modifications implemented by incorporating a U-slot into the E-shaped configuration following CMA evaluation. The antenna’s on-body performance is evaluated through cylindrical bending with varying radii, considering the proximity of a human wrist model to the antenna. The final antenna exhibits superior performance after bending, demonstrating robust gain and an expanded bandwidth compared to its initial state. Notably, the antenna achieves a maximum bandwidth of 3.73 GHz to 8.18 GHz under severe bending conditions. Under slight bending scenarios, the antenna attains a peak gain of 10.3 dBi at 5.0 GHz. Of particular significance, the antenna’s bandwidth encompasses the ISM 5.8 GHz band, positioning it as a promising candidate for Wireless Energy Harvesting (WEH) applications. Crucially, this paper validates the efficacy of Characteristic Mode Analysis in predicting the impact of bending on antennas, thereby providing valuable insights for the design of flexible and conformal antennas.

articleTitle: A Comparative Study on Magnetic Flux Density Distribution in Wireless Charging Chambers Using Rotational Method
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Power Technology Conference and Expo (WPTCE)
abstract: This paper presents a comparative study of the magnetic flux density distribution inside two shapes, namely cubic and octagonal-prism-based, wireless charging chambers controlled by the rotational method. An optimal phase difference angle for the octagonal prism-based wireless charging container is designed to be π/4. Both simulation and experiment are carried out and the results show that the octagonal-prism-based wireless charging container can realize a more even magnetic flux density distribution than the cubic one. This advancement facilitates omnidirectional wireless charging for the receivers with minimal power fluctuations.

articleTitle: Spatial Power-Splitting Metasurface for Simultaneous Wireless Information and Power Transfer
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Power Technology Conference and Expo (WPTCE)
abstract: This work proposes a novel spatial power-splitting (PS) scheme with metasurface for simultaneous wireless information and power transfer (SWIPT). A rectifying metasurface with etched ground is presented to harvest most of the RF signal while transmitting a portion of the signal. A metasurface antenna utilizing the etched ground as the radiating patches is then formed to receive the transmitted signal for communication. Therefore, the proposed metasurface realizes the separation of RF signal for dc power and information in the space domain without extra divider or coupler. Furthermore, the ratio of dc power and information can be adjusted by changing the width of the etched slot on the ground. The proposed scheme and metasurface have great potential in SWIPT applications.

articleTitle: Misalignment-Tolerant Coils for a Robust Wireless Power Transfer System
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Power Technology Conference and Expo (WPTCE)
abstract: Wireless power transfer (WPT) has demonstrated significant promise for various applications, including consumer electronics, drone charging, and mobile devices. However, misalignment between the coupling coils is a crucial issue that degrades transfer efficiency since power is transferred using an inductive coupling approach. This study presents the designed coupling coil maintains a constant mutual inductance even when the receiver coil moves freely inside the transmitter coil. This design ensures that the receiver acquires stable power from the transmitter.

articleTitle: Impact of Misalignments on the Thermal Behaviour of an IPT Coupler
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Power Technology Conference and Expo (WPTCE)
abstract: This paper compares the thermal behaviour of an inductive power transfer coupler with different compensation topologies at misaligned positions. Three commonly used compensation topologies (SS, LCC, and LCCS) are designed for a set of planar coils. Coupled electro-thermal simulations are run on the different configurations using finite element analysis (FEA) software ANSYS Maxwell to predict their thermal behaviour. LCCS compensated system is shown to have the best thermal performance with a maximum temperature of 67 °C at a misalignment of 120mm when compared to the SS: 82.3℃, and LCC: 70.56 ℃, compensated systems at a misalignment of 120mm.

articleTitle: Recurrent Neural Network-Based Charging Model of Supercapacitor for Far-Field Wireless Power Transfer
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Power Technology Conference and Expo (WPTCE)
abstract: Supercapacitors, featured for their high-power storage density, swift response, environmental sustainability, and extended lifespan, play a crucial role in energy storage applications. Despite their widespread use, the challenge of self-discharge, particularly in low-power scenarios like far-field wireless power transfer (WPT) systems, remains significant. Existing models based on parameters like maximum leakage current and equivalent series resistance (ESR) encounter limitations during voltage-variable charging, exacerbated by calculation errors. This paper proposes a novel recurrent neural network (RNN)-based charging model for predicting the charging state of supercapacitors. Trained through constant current experiments, the proposed model demonstrates effectiveness in predicting the voltage of the supercapacitor during charging period and it is validated through an experiment adopting a 915MHz voltage doubled rectifier. The presented model contributes valuable insights for optimizing far-field WPT system performance operating at microwave frequency and beyond.

articleTitle: A Highly Integrated Design of Dual-band HF Band (13.56MHz) / UHF Band (915MHz) Rectifier for Wireless Power Transfer
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Power Technology Conference and Expo (WPTCE)
abstract: In this study, we proposed a new design for a dual-band, four-stage complementary metal–oxide–semiconductor (CMOS) rectifier. A design concept based on coupling and radiation energy translation theory is employed to reuse the same rectifier circuits for both the HF band (13.56MHz) and the UHF band (915MHz) energy harvesting modes by re-configuring impedance matching between the DC and RF ports. To optimize the efficiency of the rectifier under low input voltage swing, we utilized an improved cross-coupled bridge configuration capable of boosting the input signal to improve the energy harvesting capability and driven by a differential RF input. A differential-drive active gate bias mechanism accomplishes both low ON resistance and small reverse leakage in MOS transistors with diode connections. To demonstrate the viability of the proposed design methodology, we designed a power-harvesting receiver with a dual-band, four-stage rectifier using a 0.18 um CMOS process. Within the UHF/HF frequencies, the input power range was -10 dBm to 8.5 dBm/3.5 mW, the maximum efficiency was 51.78%/40.15%, and the output DC voltage was measured at 2.85 V/2.52 V.

articleTitle: An Interleaved Class-E Resonant Inverter With Wide-Range Load for a Single-Stage Wireless DC Motor Drive
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Power Technology Conference and Expo (WPTCE)
abstract: Traditional wired DC motors often face challenges associated with cable, copper losses, and magnetic losses, which can have a notable impact on the efficiency and lifespan of the motors. These losses, arising from the nature of the wired connection, can hamper the overall performance and longevity of DC motors. This paper introduces an innovative solution to the challenges posed by traditional wired DC motors, presenting a single-stage class-E resonant wireless power transfer (WPT) technique that controls the DC motor. The proposed WPT system incorporates an interleaved wide-load class-E resonant circuit with zero-voltage switching (ZVS) characteristic at the transmitter side (Tx) to amplify the output power, enabling efficient handling of the DC motor's changing load conditions under different speeds. Meanwhile, at the receiver side (Rx), a full-bridge phase-shift (FBPS) technique is employed to modulate the phase and control the armature voltage supplied to the DC motor, thereby controlling its speed. Numerical results demonstrate that the proposed technique in this paper achieves a maximum efficiency of 91.2% at a phase shift of 180 degrees.

articleTitle: 6.78 MHz Compact Wireless Power Transfer System with Voltage Conversion from 400 V to 48 V and Integrated PCB Coils
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Power Technology Conference and Expo (WPTCE)
abstract: This paper presents the design and measurement results of a wireless power transfer (WPT) system for industrial applications. The system operates at a high switching frequency of 6.78 MHz, enabling compact coil integration into a printed circuit board (PCB). The resonant circuit is based on the LLC topology, which utilizes the mutual and stray inductances of the transmitter and receiver coils. The system achieves a power transfer of up to 450 W while reducing the input voltage from 400 V to a practical on-board voltage of 48 V. The peak efficiency is 90% at 350 W. Full zero voltage switching (ZVS) is achieved, reducing switching losses and allowing passive cooling. The innovative design combines functionality with space efficiency, making it suitable for various industrial applications.

articleTitle: Interdisciplinary Evaluation of Implant Locations for Transcutaneous Inductive Energy Transfer Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Power Technology Conference and Expo (WPTCE)
abstract: The number of donor hearts in case of severe heart failure covers only about a quarter of all patients on the waiting list. That’s why mechanical circulatory support systems are to be designed for long time use, which provide a best possible integration in daily life routine. Unfortunately, there are still weak spots regarding these devices, for example an energy transmission driveline through the abdominal wall, that can cause life threatening infections. Getting rid of this driveline is the next step in ventricular assist device improvement. Therefore, an interdisciplinary approach is very important to consider both technical and human aspects. In this paper, a setup of a transcutaneous inductive energy transfer system is presented. Its focus is on coil displacement tolerance as well as loss reduction of implanted secondary side components. Furthermore, locations for the coil implant in the human body are discussed regarding technical, anatomical and applicability-related criteria. As a result, implanting the coil subcutaneously in the upper chest is assessed as the most promising implantation area.

articleTitle: Surface Wave Power Transmission Excited on Metal Wires by Capacitive Couplers
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Power Technology Conference and Expo (WPTCE)
abstract: Transmission characteristics of electric surface waves, which propagate along a metal wire carrying electric power generated by a capacitive coupler have been studied. Capacitive couplers are wirelessly coupled in the near field, the transmission efficiency drops sharply as the distance increases in the air. On the other hand, by coupling a capacitive coupler to a metal wire and propagating the power radiated from the capacitive coupler as surface waves on the metal wire, the transmission distance can be extended more than one hundred times. The resonant frequency of the coupler considered in this study is 2.45 GHz. Experiments and electromagnetic field simulations were carried out to confirm how the transmission efficiency varies by changing the length, thickness, and material of the metal wire as a guide of the surface wave.

articleTitle: Integration of Solar Energy and Power Management in Portable Transmitter for WPT
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Power Technology Conference and Expo (WPTCE)
abstract: This paper describes the development and initial validation of a portable architecture for Wireless Power Transmission (WPT) systems. The central component of this architecture is the TX powered by a battery that is charged through solar panels, which embodies both sustainability and portability. The system includes a custom-designed Power Management Unit (PMU) and an active bias controller, providing control over the power amplifier and managing power flow from solar panels to the battery and then to the WPT system. The versatility of the architecture is demonstrated by its potential applicability in various scenarios, ranging from remote sensor networks to the integration in Solar Power Satellites (SPS).

articleTitle: Enhancing Wireless Power Transfer Efficiency for Implantable Medical Devices Using Metamaterial
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Power Technology Conference and Expo (WPTCE)
abstract: Increasing the wireless power transfer efficiency (PTE) is crucial for implementing implantable medical devices (IMDs). The challenge in powering such implants stems from the human brain tissue’s elevated permittivity, conductivity, and mass density, which pose difficulties across high frequencies. This study introduces a metamaterial-based near-field wireless power transfer (WPT) system. It evaluates its performance against traditional WPT systems with a 36×36 mm transmitter and 900×485 um receiver coil. The size of the metamaterial unit cell is 12×12 mm. Numerical analysis reveals that the S21 parameter of the metamaterial-based WPT system shows a 4.21 dB enhancement over the conventional WPT system at 200 MHz, specifically for an ultra-small receiver coil. From the specific absorption rate simulation, it can be found that maximum transmitted power improved by more than 2.4 times due to the distance between the transmitter coil and tissue stack. Additionally, a comparative analysis involving magnetic fields has been conducted to deepen the understanding of the power transfer mechanism. Moreover, a comparative study has been provided with a recent metamaterial-based WPT system for IMDs. The proposed system demonstrates the potential for use in neural implants, offering an improved PTE.

articleTitle: Experimental Verification of EMI Reduction in Dynamic Wireless Power Transfer System Using Soft-Switching Active Bridge Converter
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Power Technology Conference and Expo (WPTCE)
abstract: This paper demonstrates the effectiveness of the proposed soft-switching active bridge converter in dynamic wireless power transfer (DWPT) systems. In experiments, it was confirmed that the prototype converter operated with soft switching during DWPT. In addition, the efficiency of the proposed system was enhanced by 2.3 percentage points on average compared to a system using a conventional converter. Furthermore, the proposed system reduced radiated electromagnetic interference (EMI) by 5.8 dBμV on average.

articleTitle: Measurement of Electrical Characteristics of Vehicle Body Toward Capacitive Power Transfer Through Automotive Paintings
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Power Technology Conference and Expo (WPTCE)
abstract: In this paper, impedance characteristics of real car body is measured toward implementation of capacitive power transfer through automotive paintings. In measurement of car impedance, capacitive coupling electrodes are applied at three different positions in order to observe impedance characteristics changed for different positions. After measurement, equivalent circuit at the different electrode positions are estimated for realization of further efficient capacitive power transfer.

articleTitle: Quality Factor Comparison of Pipe Coils in Wireless Charging Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Power Technology Conference and Expo (WPTCE)
abstract: This paper investigates the quality factor of copper tube power transfer coils made of highly conductive metal pipes and contributes to their potential use in inductive charging systems. Instead of the most common stranded litz wire windings, pipes are a very cost-effective alternative that also provide an integrated cooling option. In principle, this makes their use interesting for applications with active cooling, e.g. due to high transfer power, or in applications with exceptional cost pressure, e.g. due to scaling effects of road electrification in dynamic wireless charging. At the same time, solid tubes show a strong frequency dependence of the current density distribution, which has impact on their potential power transfer efficiency. In this paper, the achievable coil quality factor of tubular coils is investigated in order to decide whether their cost advantage outweighs the loss of efficiency in respect to litz wire. For this purpose, both aluminum and copper pipes are compared.

articleTitle: Coils Parallelization: A Strategy for Improving Power Transfer Efficiency and Specific Absorption Rate in Wireless Power Transfer System for Implantable Medical Devices
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Power Technology Conference and Expo (WPTCE)
abstract: This paper proposes a new single-turn coil design to improve Wireless Power Transfer (WPT) for brain implantable medical devices (IMDs). Our approach considers both near-field propagation and tissue interaction, primarily maximizing power transfer efficiency (PTE) while minimizing specific absorption rate (SAR). We present methods to adjust the feed line using Grounded Coplanar Waveguide (GCPW) and reduce coil impedance through the parallelization of coils, resulting in a reduction in electric field (E-field) and enhancement of magnetic field (H-field), thereby yielding superior PTE performance and SAR reduction. Furthermore, we investigate the optimized distance of the transmitter coil to the tissue, clarifying the crucial role of coil positioning in maximizing quality factor (Q factor) while minimizing SAR. Our proposed techniques are validated through simulations, showcasing a remarkable improvement in the maximum allowable transmitted power up to 23% and an increase in H-field up to 8% compared to conventional coil designs. The combination of coil parallelization and the capacitor segmentation method offers 35% of enhancements to the SAR. Additionally, this coil parallelization approach alleviates the undesirable H-field attenuation encountered with the capacitor segmentation technique, which is attributed to the ESR of additional capacitors.

articleTitle: Live Coupling Coefficient Calculation Method for Capacitive Wireless Power Transfer with Multiple Receivers
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Power Technology Conference and Expo (WPTCE)
abstract: Capacitive wireless power transfer shows promise for wireless energy delivery, utilizing capacitive coupling for transmission. Quantifying the coupling between individual transmitters and receivers is essential, as optimization techniques for optimal output impedance depend on accurate knowledge of the coupling coefficient. Methods to measure this coupling exist, but these are applied to a specific configuration of a capacitive power transfer system, requiring a new measurement each time the distance or alignment between transmitters and receivers change. Since practical capacitive power transfer systems often experience variations in distance or alignment, impacting the coupling coefficient and consequently, the optimal output impedance, it is desired to constantly measure the coupling coefficient. This paper proposes a concise, exact method for live coupling coefficient calculation, and looks into the application of this method for systems with one transmitter and one receiver, and one transmitter and multiple receivers.

articleTitle: Realizing interference-free far-field measurement of large-scale energy emission arrays with photonic antennas
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Power Technology Conference and Expo (WPTCE)
abstract: Here, we propose a photonic antenna with an electro-optical micro-resonator that can be used as an electric field vector detector and avoid electromagnetic disturbance. With the help of the photonic antenna, the far-field electromagnetic field distribution and beam direction from the large-scale energy emission arrays can be measured accurately and undisturbed.

articleTitle: An Ultra-Wide Bandwidth with Compact Size Implantable Antenna for Health Monitor Microsystem
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Power Technology Conference and Expo (WPTCE)
abstract: In this study, an ultra-wide bandwidth with compact volume implantable antenna in the applications health monitor microsystem is proposed. A biocompatible, stable and high efficiency material, the Rogers 3010 ( ε<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">r</inf> = 10.2 and loss tangent of σ = 0.001) with thickness of 0.25 mm is employed as the substrate. The proposed antenna with compact size of 9 mm × 9 mm × 0.5 mm (40.5 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>) with an ultra-wide impedance matching of 5380 MHz (1.42 GHz - 6.8 GHz). The ultra-wide bandwidth characteristic of the antenna is achieved by introducing a simple antenna with the patch based on metamaterial unit-cell and the cutting flower slots as well as several semicirculars on the ground plane. The proposed antenna’s performances are tested via numerical simulations in a skin phantom model with the frequency-dependent electrical properties. Furthermore, the antenna provides low specific absorption rate (SAR) values that comply with IEEE safety guidelines.

articleTitle: Synchronous Tuning of Self-Oscillating for Electrical Coupled Bidirectional Wireless Power Transfer System
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Power Technology Conference and Expo (WPTCE)
abstract: Electrical Coupled Bidirectional Wireless Power Transfer System (EC-BWPT) system has gradually attracted attention due to the unique advantages of transferring power through metal barriers, lightweight structure, which achieving bidirectional wireless power transmission between the power grid and electrical equipments. However, due to the high operating frequency of the EC-BWPT system, frquency and phase synchronization of the primary and secondary independent controllers is crucial for achieving precise bidirectional power transmission. This paper proposes a self-oscillation synchronous tuning control technology for the bilateral LCLC resonant network EC-BWPT system, the stable ZVS operating points of self-oscillating are derived by stroboscopic mapping and Poincare mapping models, and then the controllers driving the converters by detecting zero crossing resonant current of the primary and secondary sides. The implementation of the control method does not require PLL, VCO, complex data calculations, additional analog circuits, complex control algorithms, etc. The simulation validated the effectiveness of the proposed self-oscillation synchronous tuning control method for the proposed EC-BWPT system.

Author Keywords: Electrical Coupled Bidirectional Wireless Power Transfer System

articleTitle: Experimental Study of Realizing a Low-Noise Injection-Locked Magnetron Based on a Switch-Mode Power Supply
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Power Technology Conference and Expo (WPTCE)
abstract: Injection-locked magnetrons (ILMGT) are potential candidates in various industrial applications, for example, wireless power transmission. Generally, the output phase and amplitude stability of an ILMGT are influenced by the voltage or current ripple of its power supply. Thus, a high-performance ILMGT cannot exist without an excellent power supply. Switch-mode power supply (SMPS) has the advantages of being compact, high-efficiency, and high-controllability, but it also has a high-ripple and noisy output. Our study is to depress anode voltage ripple without excessive volume and complexity increase. A novel ripple reduction method is proposed. The peak-to-peak value of the SMPS’s voltage ripple is reduced from 282 V to 29 V. The output phase jitter of the ILMGT is suppressed from 49° to 0.7° when the injection ratio is 0.13. Besides, the 100-Hz noise is almost completely eliminated without any 100-Hz LC filter. This study provides a reference to establish a compact and low-noise ILMGT system based on commercial SMPSs.

articleTitle: Power Flow Control and ZVS Condition Analysis in Multiport Wireless Energy Router
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Power Technology Conference and Expo (WPTCE)
abstract: This paper comprehensively analyzes the power transfer characteristics and soft-switching conditions of a multiport wireless power transfer system in the presence of cross-coupling, and proposes a port-equivalent method to address the relationship between power demands, soft switching conditions and the control variables. First, a system architecture with vertical stacking of coupling coils is presented and its power flow characteristics are analyzed. Then, based on a time-domain model of the system considering higher harmonics, the instantaneous currents at the switching moment of the power switches are derived and the soft switching conditions are analyzed. The relationship between output power and soft switching conditions are established, and a port-equivalent method is proposed to simplify the system analysis. Finally, a 76W one-to-three port prototype is built and used to verify the theoretical analysis.

articleTitle: A Front-end Coupling Coefficient Estimation Method for the S-LCC Compensated Wireless Power Transfer Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Power Technology Conference and Expo (WPTCE)
abstract: This paper proposes a fast and accurate front-end monitoring method to estimate the coupling coefficient in the series (S)-LCC compensated wireless power transfer (WPT) systems. The proposed method can be implemented with only one sensor for the phase information detection of the transmitter current, without requiring any information on the receiver side. A fast frequency-sweeping process is used to obtain the zero-phase-angle frequencies of the WPT systems with the load disconnected. Detailed control algorithm is provided. Experimental results are included to verify that the proposed method can estimate the coupling coefficients within 6 ms while maintaining high accuracies. The largest estimation error is only 1.47%.

articleTitle: A Hybrid Detector Array for Simultaneous Detection of Living and Metal Object in Wireless Power Transfer Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Power Technology Conference and Expo (WPTCE)
abstract: This paper proposed a sensing unit of Foreign Object Detection (FOD) for Wireless Power Transfer (WPT) systems that works for both Metal Object Detection (MOD) and Living Object Detection (LOD). Based on the proposed sensing unit, an adaptive excitation and detection algorithm is presented, where the exicitation signal with selectable frequencies components is generated to improve the detection rate of random Metal and Living Objects (MOs and LOs). Using the proposed sensing unit and the detection algorthm, the detection system works like a simplified impedance analyzer, which ultilizing the equivalent LC network of sensing unit as probe to detect the impedance variation due to the inductive coupling between MO and sensing unit’s coil, as well as the capacitive coupling between LO and sensing unit’s copper strip. Compared with conventional MOD and LOD systems, the detection system in this work has the advantages of reduced system complexity (using one sensing unit for both MOD and LOD, thus only one signal processing path is necessary) and improved sensitivity, especially in weak detection positions (e.g. boundaries of sensing components).

articleTitle: Wearable Electromagnetic Halbach Array for Wirelessly Charging Implantable Biomedical Devices
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Power Technology Conference and Expo (WPTCE)
abstract: This paper presents a wearable hexagon-shaped Electromagnetic Halbach Array designed for wirelessly charging implantable biomedical devices. The coils are made of liz wires and the transmitting coil is sewn onto the canvas fabric to make it more wearable. Through electromagnetic simulations and experimental investigations, the effectiveness of wireless power transmission has been demonstrated. A fully integrated EHA wireless power transfer system including coils and its tuning capacitors has been investigated. The test was carried out in both air and saline environment. Experimentally, it was found that the proposed system can transmit a maximum of 1.8W and 1.59W of power in the air and saline, respectively, with a maximum efficiency of 1.35% and 1.19%, respectively.

articleTitle: A Novel Concentrator Design for OMEGA Wireless Power Transmission System
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Power Technology Conference and Expo (WPTCE)
abstract: This paper proposes an umbrella-type foldable concentrator for the Orb-shape Membrane Energy Gathering Array (OMEGA) space solar power station. This design is inspired by the umbrella-like collapsible antenna and is used to achieve a lightweight and highly stowable OMEGA space solar power station. This concentrator is composed of a rigid reflective surface intercepted from the center of the spherical crown and a thin film reflective surface formed by several curved ribs. The analysis of axial error indicates that reducing the concentrator aperture and the number of ribs results in a smaller axial root mean square error. To achieve the required precision of 3.6-5.4 mm, the minimum of 48 ribs is necessary. The number of ribs was reduced to 12 to improve deployment reliability. The solar array profile was optimized to compensate for the error. A crank-like slider mechanism was designed to achieve simultaneous deployment of the array and the thin-film reflective surface. Modal analysis was performed on the concentrator to obtain the inherent frequency required for the design. The resonant frequency of the concentrator can meet the design requirements.

articleTitle: A Dual Sided Power Regulation Control Strategy for a 50 kW Inductive Power Transfer EV Charger
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Power Technology Conference and Expo (WPTCE)
abstract: This paper proposes an efficient power regulation control method for a high-power LCL-LCL tuned Inductive Power Transfer (IPT) Wireless Charging System (WCS) using a Duel Active Bridge (DAB) topology. A combination of conduction angle and active bridge phase shift control is used to maintain Zero-Voltage Switching (ZVS) on both the primary and secondary side when moderate power regulation is required. A first-harmonic analysis of the LCL-LCL system is presented which shows the functionality of the control method. Experimental results are presented when delivering 50 kW of power under high coupling conditions. These show reduced switching losses in the active bridges and a dc-dc system efficiency increase of 0.7 % using the proposed control method.

articleTitle: Development of 2.4 GHz Phased Array Transmitter For Wireless Power Transfer
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Power Technology Conference and Expo (WPTCE)
abstract: A four-element phased array transmitter is developed for wireless power transfer at 2.4 GHz. The transmitting beam is formed by the radiation patterns of four patch antennas. The measured gain of the phased array antenna at the angle of 0 degrees is 8.9 dBi with a 3-dB beamwidth of 21 degrees. The beam can be steered from +45° to -45°, achieving a minimum resolution of 1 degree, with the phase shift control of 4 digital bits on the individual RF phase shifter. The maximum equivalent isotropically radiated power is about 38 dBm.

articleTitle: Coupling Estimation of Wireless Power Transfer Systems with Constant Voltage Load Through Zero-Phase Angle Frequency
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Power Technology Conference and Expo (WPTCE)
abstract: This paper proposes a coupling estimation method for wireless power transfer (WPT) systems with constant voltage load (CVL). The method involves calculating the zero-phase angle (ZPA) frequencies, which are found to be solely dependent on the coupling and independent of the output voltage in WPT systems with CVL and frequency bifurcation. By leveraging this unique characteristic, a self-oscillation method is employed to automatically locate the ZPA points, enabling rapid and accurate coupling estimation. The proposed method is highly effective across the entire range of couplings and does not require wireless communication, additional hardware, or complex calculations. Simulation results are provided to validate the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Highly Integrated Wireless Power Transfer System for an Inductive Electrically Excited Synchronous Machine
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Power Technology Conference and Expo (WPTCE)
abstract: In this paper a highly integrated wireless power transfer system intended to replace the slip rings of an electrically excited synchronous machine is proposed. The loosely coupled ferrite-less rotary transformer as well as the secondary side power electronics are placed into the rotor hollow shaft of the machine. In addition to the compact construction, the design also focuses on enhancements in efficiency, mechanical stability and the cooling of the WPT system. Moreover, the use of a hollow shaft made out of glass fiber reinforced plastic reduces the necessary installation space significantly. The laboratory measurements demonstrate that in an installation space of less than 0.3 l a power of 2.5 kW is transmitted with a peak efficiency of 95 % at a frequency of 350 kHz.

articleTitle: Suppression of Leakage Current in DWPT Systems Using 3-Legged Inverters by Pulse Width and Phase Adjustment
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Power Technology Conference and Expo (WPTCE)
abstract: EV dynamic charging systems using 3-legged inverters have been proposed to reduce the implementation costs of wireless power transfer systems. A novel switching method is proposed to suppress undesirable leakage current in stand-by inductors in such systems through pulse width and phase adjustment of gate signals of stand-by legs. Leakage current and EMF suppression of the proposed method were verified in experiments.

articleTitle: Differential Inductive Positioning System for Wireless Charging as Extension for the Standards to a Multi Ground Assembly Parking Spot with "No Preselection" as Enabler for Market Breakthrough
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Power Technology Conference and Expo (WPTCE)
abstract: In wireless charging for light duty vehicles, three of the four key interoperability topics (coil system, operating point, communication, and positioning) have been defined for some time. Positioning is the last cornerstone that is still missing for a complete standard description. The Differential Inductive Positioning System (DIPS) has established itself as the standard procedure within the SAE J2954 standard. Positioning is the main experience that the end customer has with wireless charging, as the actual charging process can only be perceived via visual signals. A closer look at this end customer experience reveals that all wireless charging standards (SAE, IEC, ISO, GB) have so far only considered charging in a parking lot with one ground assembly unit. And a data connection between VA and GA is established before the actual positioning process. As a result, it is not possible for the driver to freely select a parking space. Instead, the respective parking space must be selected before driving into it. A preselection would be very unintuitive also when it is regarded to roll out the alignment method for dynamic wireless charging as well. With DIPS a solution has been presented for this, which has been adopted in SAE J2954. DIPS makes it possible for the driver to park freely without having to preselect a parking space e.g., on the display. This additional degree of freedom is a great benefit for the driver's comfort, which can be a push for the market breakthrough of wireless charging for light-duty vehicles and thus for electromobility in general.

articleTitle: General Dynamic Gyrator Models for Transient Analysis of IPT
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Power Technology Conference and Expo (WPTCE)
abstract: An innovative dynamic gyrator model is proposed for transient analysis of inductive power transfer(IPT). The well-known dynamic phasor is applied to a magnetically coupled model of IPT and then a dynamic gyrator is derived from the phasor domain circuit. Similar to a static gyrator, the dynamic gyrator has an imaginary gain; however, it is valid not only for the steady state but also for the transient state. It is verified that IPT with two LC resonant tanks of the fourth order system is degenerated to the second order system. Dynamic control of transient IPT circuit was tremendously difficult due to very high order compensation circuits of IPT systems. Any IPT systems regardless of the types of compensation circuits can be analyzed by the proposed dynamic gyrator. Simulation for a series-series compensated IPT of 100W tuned at 100 kHz successfully verified the proposed dynamic gyrator model.

articleTitle: The Novel Flexible Fresnel Lens on PET Substrate
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Power Technology Conference and Expo (WPTCE)
abstract: In this paper, the authors present the first design of a Fresnel Zone Lens (FZL) on a flexible dielectric substrate, namely Polyethylene terephthalate (PET), operating at 28 GHz. Notably, the FZL exhibits broadband performance across the range of 25-30 GHz. The far-field radiation patterns of the horn antenna are plotted both without the lens and with the FZL, bent at various central bending angles (θ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">b</inf>). The FZL demonstrates stable performance, with the realized gain of the horn antenna decreasing by an average of 0.13 dBi and 0.93 dBi for θ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">b</inf> =50° and 120°, respectively. This discovery suggests potential applications in fields such as vehicle communication and biomedical applications, where conformal surfaces are prevalent, enabling efficient wireless power transfer.

articleTitle: Double-Layer Three-Phase Resonator for High-Power Wireless Power Transfer
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Power Technology Conference and Expo (WPTCE)
abstract: Recently, high-power wireless power transfer (WPT) technology for fast battery charging in applications such as electric vehicles has been actively researched. This paper presents a novel three-phase resonator as a crucial technology for high-power wireless power transfer systems. The proposed resonator’s leakage magnetic field, efficiency, voltage, and current characteristics are compared with those of a conventional single-phase resonator, aiming to assess its suitability for high-power wireless charging applications. The analysis is performed by comparing a three-phase resonator with a single-phase resonator of the same diameter using the electromagnetic (EM) simulation tool. The results showed that the three-phase resonator generates less leakage magnetic field and lower secondary current than the single-phase resonator when the distance between the resonators is close. It was shown that the three-phase resonator is more advantageous in terms of human safety compliance and receiver weight reduction. This paper shows how resonator design can address leakage magnetic field concerns and system limitations in high-power WPT system design.

articleTitle: Energy harvesting feasibility for safety belt buckle
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Power Technology Conference and Expo (WPTCE)
abstract: Technology is to an increasing degree becoming spatially distributed, as Internet of Things or sensors in vehicles. With this comes challenges in power supply, with either cumbersome amounts of batteries or power cables. In this paper we examine the potential of energy harvesting for powering a safety sensor on a belt buckle. Concluding that that the vibrations on this site are impractically small, we propose an energy harvester for transducing human induced mechanical energy. The electromagnetic energy harvester converts vertical buckle-in/-out events into rotations of a circular array of magnets, varying the flux through a coil. Both measurements and simulations are performed, the later showing a potential energy of 4mJ for a single buckle-in event.

articleTitle: Accuracy Improvement of Impedance Measurement for Nonlinear Devices
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Power Technology Conference and Expo (WPTCE)
abstract: Impedance measurement for nonlinear devices is important in designing and tuning a system of wireless power transfer. Hence, this study has made preliminary contributions to the construction of an integrated real-time nonlinear impedance measurement system. Firstly, building upon previous work, this research deeply explores a nonlinear load impedance measurement method using only a directional coupler and an oscilloscope. Subsequently, addressing practical application scenarios, a calibration method based on the S-parameters of the directional coupler is proposed, further enhancing measurement accuracy. Finally, all data processing is encapsulated into a software, laying the foundation for future development of an integrated real-time measurement system.

articleTitle: Simultaneous Wireless Power and Information Transfer System With Capacitive Coupler Based on Differential Diplexer
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Power Technology Conference and Expo (WPTCE)
abstract: This paper proposes a differential diplexers-based capacitive wireless power and information transfer (WPIT) system for achieving maintenance-free industrial robots. The differential diplexer is designed by combining a high-pass filter (HPF) for 2.45 GHz signals, a low-pass filter (LPF) for 13.56 MHz power transfer, and an LC balun for differential output. Through the incorporation of matching with the capacitive coupler, the diplexer achieves a power transmission efficiency of 93.7% and power isolation of 60 dB. Furthermore, successful demodulation and modulation of 16QAM signals within a 1 MHz bandwidth are demonstrated, resulting in a communication speed of 4 Mbps.

articleTitle: A Distance-Independent Wireless Charging System With Hybrid Topology and Control
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Power Technology Conference and Expo (WPTCE)
abstract: This paper proposes a distance-independent wireless charging system that achieves constant current (CC) and constant voltage (CV) output through utilization of a reconfigurable topology, capable of seamlessly switching between a two-coil and a three-coil configuration. In order to enhance output adjustability and improve the efficiency of the charging process, this system combines the advantages of fractional-order and integer-order resonant circuits. In the two-coil configuration, the output of the inverter on the transmitter side is modulated as that of a fractional-order capacitor. By analyzing frequency characteristics of the fractional-order circuit, a control strategy of variable fractional order is introduced to achieve CC output against variations of transfer distance based on a mutual inductance recognition method. After transitioning to the three-coil configuration, the system inherently achieves a CV output by operating the inverter at a fixed frequency and forming an integer-order resonant circuit. In addition, in both mentioned configurations, the full-bridge (FB) mode and half-bridge (HB) mode of the inverter are utilized to minimize switching losses and broaden the range of soft-switching operation, catering to various load conditions. Finally, an experimental prototype is built to achieve CC and CV output within a wide charging range.

articleTitle: Silicon Carbide Based Power Efficienct, Compact, and Extended Range Wireless Power Transfer System for Robotic Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Power Technology Conference and Expo (WPTCE)
abstract: Wireless power transfer (WPT) is an emerging technology with applications spanning various power levels, ranging from low power level for mobile devices charging to high power rating for electric vehicle (EV) charging. While numerous studies have been conducted in these domains, there are relatively less research efforts and market products focusing on the medium power range applications such as automated guided vehicles (AGVs). In this work, an inductive coupling wireless power transfer (ICWPT) system is introduced to address the coupled electrical-thermal challenges for further enhancing power density, power efficiency, and charging distance with misalignment tolerance concurrently, which are achieved by leveraging 3D integration and packaging technologies, customize-designed driver-integrated wide bandgap power semiconductors silicon carbide (SiC) MOSFETs power modules, and a self-derived dynamic feedback algorithm (DFA) control. Detailed overall system architecture, circuit operation, and control methodology will be discussed. A 1 kW ICWPT experimental prototype is built and verified that the power density of power receiving unit, the maximum grid-to-rectifier power efficiency, and charging distance are respectively further improved to 0.6 W/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>, ≥ 90%, and 10 cm. A demonstration of wireless charging an AGV is illustrated to prove the feasibility and effectiveness of proposed ideas.

articleTitle: A Beamforming Antenna using Analog Phase Shifter for 5.7GHz RF Wireless Power Transfer System
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Power Technology Conference and Expo (WPTCE)
abstract: This article presents a prototype of a beamforming antenna integrated with a reflective phase shifter used for wireless power transfer at 5.7 GHz. Following the fabrication of discrete components—the Wilkinson splitter, a reflective phase shifter, and a square microstrip antenna—on an FR-4 board, we integrate them as a phased array antenna and assess the characteristics of beam steering. The Wilkinson splitter exhibited a 2 dB attenuation beyond the ideal threshold. Despite the intention to secure a 135-degree phase shift for beam direction control within ±45 degrees using the reflective phase shifter employing a 90-degree hybrid and a varactor, the achieved phase shift plateaued at 46 degrees, enabling a maximum steering of ±15 degrees. The authors clarify the relationship between the applied voltage value for the varactor and the quantities of phase shift in this experiment. A 4-element square microstrip array antenna is capable to maintain an S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf> of -10 dB or lower in the 5.7 GHz band. The proposed phased array antenna is an integration of them, and its radiation pattern is measured by setting the quantity of the phase shifts obtained by the preceding experiment. The measurement results, unfortunately differs from our expected one at this stage.

articleTitle: Analysis and LEDs Illumination Using Wi-Fi Tethering of Novel Crossed Dipole Rectenna Array
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Power Technology Conference and Expo (WPTCE)
abstract: This study proposes a novel cross-dipole type rectenna array that utilizes the lead wires of two LEDs and rectifying diodes as half-wavelength dipole antennas for horizontal and vertical directions, respectively. The 10 rectenna elements are arranged with a spacing of 15 mm, and the wireless power transmission efficiency is evaluated for each rectenna acting as a receiving element. Results reveal that the wireless power transmission efficiency gradually decreases as the distance between them increases without the arrayed rectennas between the transmitting and receiving elements. However, the wireless power transmission efficiency remains nearly constant even with an increased distance between the transmitting and receiving elements with the rectennas arranged in an array. Furthermore, experiments using leaking waves from a microwave oven demonstrate the ability to simultaneously illuminate 16 LEDs with a distance of 105 mm from the wave source to the most distant element. Additionally, successful activation of LEDs on rectennas located 150 mm away from the wave source is achieved when the array of cross-dipole type rectennas is used for radio waves generated by Wi-Fi tethering mode.

articleTitle: Magnetic Field Analysis of Curved-Surface Coils for High-Spatial-Freedom WPT
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Power Technology Conference and Expo (WPTCE)
abstract: The MHz Wireless Power Transfer (WPT) is known to have the advantages of further transfer distance and extra convenience. A combination of multiple coils and some modulation methodologies provide improved spatial freedom. However, research on coil designs and array applications for confined areas still lacks consideration. This article studies the characteristics of curved-surface coils in magnetic field shaping. Focusing on a specific cylindrical surface, the curved-surface coils are analyzed and optimized, aiming to provide stable output inside the cylindrical space when both lateral and angular misalignment happen. The magnetic field density generated by a curved-surface coil is mathematically derived. Relevant simulations are conducted in HFSS to verify the field shaping effects. A 6.78 MHz system is setup to test the power transfer performance. One planar coil and one curved-surface coil with identical size are compared in the experiment. The results show improved stability of power transfer when both lateral and angular misalignment exist.

articleTitle: Side-Variant Active Shielding Coils for High Power Wireless Charging Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Power Technology Conference and Expo (WPTCE)
abstract: A side-variant active shielding method for wireless power transfer (WPT) systems is proposed in this paper. It consists of four separate shielding coils; two on the ground assembly and two on the vehicle assembly with one on each lateral side of the car. The general idea is to operate these side-variant active shielding coils so that effective shielding is achieved where needed.
