At the same time, overcompensation by exceeding the required leakage field reduction should be avoided, as this can result in lower system efficiencies. The proposed side-variant active shielding method is applied to a 50 kW WPT system and demonstrated for different positions. The simulation results show the shielding method’s effectiveness and its capability to enlarge the operating range of a WPT system. As different shielding coil combinations can be used for the same position, the proposed side-variant active shielding method enables an additional degree of freedom for the system operation.

articleTitle: A New Current-fed Inductive Wireless Charging Transmitter for Large-scale EV In-motion Wireless Charging Infrastructure
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Power Technology Conference and Expo (WPTCE)
abstract: Large-scale in-motion inductive wireless charging infrastructure could be a key enabler for widespread adoption of electric vehicles (EVs) leading to net-zero carbon emissions for the transportation sector. However, the challenge of distributing power to the numerous transmitters in such large-scale systems has not been adequately investigated. This paper presents further development of a patented novel power distribution architecture that provides improved system efficiency, reliability, and cost in large-scale EV in-motion wireless charging systems. This paper provides details on operation and analysis of the proposed current-fed wireless charging transmitter. The proposed transmitter achieves load-independent transmitter coil current and high tolerance to mistuning. Simulation results from a 1 kW current-fed transmitter design validate the proposed design and analysis.

articleTitle: Load-Independent Dual-Frequency Constant-Current and Constant-Voltage Wireless Power Transfer System for Multiple Pickups
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Power Technology Conference and Expo (WPTCE)
abstract: The wireless charging technique for multiple pickups under the same electromagnetic field is deemed a convenient, simple, and compatible power supply approach, which is undergoing exponential growth. However, some concerns are emerging against this background: 1) Different operating frequencies of various charging standards pose challenges to the design of impedance matching network; 2) The wireless charging system hardly realizes constant-current (CC) or constant-voltage (CV) output characteristics under various charging frequencies. Hence, this paper presents and proposes a load-independent dual-frequency compensation topology to realize CC of both resonant frequencies on the primary side. Meanwhile, by adopting the proposed hybrid compensation network on the pickup side, both CC and CV can be satisfied according to the demand for devices. Moreover, a communication-free method for controlling the hybrid compensation network is also introduced. Verification results will be given to testify the feasibility and effectiveness of the proposed system.

articleTitle: Impedance Based Interoperability Comparison of Active and Passive Rectification Topologies for Wireless EV Charging Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Power Technology Conference and Expo (WPTCE)
abstract: For the widespread adoption of Wireless Power Transfer (WPT) systems for electric vehicle (EV) charging, the development of interoperable systems and bidirectional power transfer is of key interest. While existing standardization efforts have focused on unidirectional power transfer, this paper explores the potential of incorporating an active rectification (AR) topology on the vehicle side to enable bidirectional power transfer. Specifically, new sets of electronics for the 10 kW SAE J2954 reference vehicle assemblies (VAs) are investigated and their impact on interoperability is assessed. The study demonstrated that AR offers promising advantages, including increased interoperability and efficiency, while eliminating the need for tunable matching networks.

articleTitle: A High-Efficiency Wireless Power Transfer System With Variable Capacitor Technique for Compensating Coil Misalignment
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Power Technology Conference and Expo (WPTCE)
abstract: This paper introduces a novel variable capacitor module (VCM) for a wireless power transfer (WPT) systems system. It operates based on the principle that ceramic capacitance changes with the variation of DC bias voltage. By generating a controllable pulse current through a driver circuit, the capacitor bias voltage can be adjusted, thereby altering the compensation capacitance to enhance system stability. In comparison to previous literature, the proposed module features a simple circuit topology with fewer circuit components, and also the power switch in the driver circuit exhibits zero-current switching (ZCS) characteristics, further reducing circuit power losses. To validate the feasibility of the proposed concept, this paper implemented a 200W WPT system. The VCM adjusts the compensation capacitance of the transmitter side (Tx) coil to achieve optimal transmission efficiency. The experimental results demonstrate that the VCM has an adjustment range of 105nF to 122nF. By using VCM, the overall system efficiency achieves an improvement of 2.74% in coil misalignment conditions and approximately 3% enhancement in resonant tank power transfer efficiency. When the coils are precisely aligned, the system can achieve an efficiency of 87%. Employing the proposed full-bridge phase shift modulation technique ensures stable control of the output voltage at 48V. Based on test results, highlighting its reliable performance.

articleTitle: MIMO-DWPT With Active Reflection Canceller
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Power Technology Conference and Expo (WPTCE)
abstract: WPT (Wireless Power Transmission) is attracting attention as a technology for reducing the battery weight of electric vehicles (EVs) and suppressing the peak power demand. To improve the transmission efficiency of wireless power transmission (WPT) in EVs, we focus on multi-input multi-output WPT (MIMO-WPT) using multiple transmitting and receiving coils. In this paper, we propose a method to cancel reflected waves that cause degradation of transmission efficiency by controlling the amplitude and phase of the RF power supply connected to the MIMO-WPT system using S-parameters without considering inter-coil coupling due to impedance matching. Electromagnetic field simulation results show that the proposed method can improve efficiency by about 60% compared to the conventional method when the air gap is 10mm.

articleTitle: Design and Analysis of a New Configuration for LCC-LCC-Compensated WPT System Using Bilateral Absolute Phase Shift Control
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Power Technology Conference and Expo (WPTCE)
abstract: This paper presents a new configuration of LCC-LCC compensation network for Wireless Power Transfer (WPT) system with active full-bridges on both sides. WPT system equipped with active full-bridges on both sides has higher control flexibility, such as phase shift control on each full-bridge and phase difference control between inverter and rectifier which also enables the bidirectional power transfer. Based on our previous works that realized the synchronization and joint control of inverter and active rectifier utilizing integrated near-field-based communication, we re-configurated the LCC-LCC-compensation in this work so that the WPT system can achieve improvements in terms of power factor, ac-efficiency and wider zero-voltage-switching area for the range of control parameters (triple phase shift control) and system parameter (coupling factor) variations. A comparison with the conventional LCC-LCC-configuration is given.

articleTitle: A Dual-Function Rectifier-Mixer Circuit for Sub-Carrier Backscattering Modulation Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Power Technology Conference and Expo (WPTCE)
abstract: ZeroPower IoT devices are a class of wireless sensors that are extremely low power and self-sustained in energy. Completely passive sensors, such as the reed switch sensor, are ideal candidates for such applications.However, in a back-scattering communication scheme, the switching should be sustained (dynamic, continuous switching) to yield any valuable modulation, which excludes many sensor switch scenarios.This paper proposes a rectifier-powered sub-carrier modulation scheme capable of differentiating the static switch positions and operating below 200mV and 0.26mW of harvested power. The designed system comprises an antenna, an oscillator, and an RF-DC converter. The characteristics of the tunnel diode are harnessed to design an extra low-power oscillator, while the non-linearities of the Schottky diode are utilized to create both rectification (RF-to-DC) and modulation functions. In this scheme, the sub-carrier LO frequency can be hardware-tuned for tag identification.

articleTitle: A Parallel-Connected Tunable Matching Network and Impedance Compression Network for Inductive Charging of Electric Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Power Technology Conference and Expo (WPTCE)
abstract: Designing IPT EV charging systems to deliver constant power is a nontrivial task, as power delivery depends on multiple factors that vary during operation, namely coupling factor and battery voltage. In response, this abstract proposes a novel IPT EV charging system that combines a ZCN with a TMN connected in parallel with the secondary pad to handle changes in both coupling factor and battery voltage respectively. This configuration uses fewer switches and passive elements than other similar systems. Simulation results of a 7.5 kW system show that the proposed system can easily compensate for up to a two-times change in coupling factor in conjunction with a 1.5-times change in battery voltage.

articleTitle: A Bi-Directional Inductive Power Transfer System with Zero Voltage Switching and Unity Power Factor for a Wide Operating Range
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Power Technology Conference and Expo (WPTCE)
abstract: A conventional bi-directional inductive power transfer (Bd-IPT) system is required to accommodate a wide range of loads due to variations in the magnetic coupling factor and battery voltage of electric vehicles (EVs). To address this challenge, the system adjusts both internal and relative phase shifts of the H-Bridge converter to achieve the desired power transfer. However, altering the internal phase shift may lead to a loss of zero-voltage switching (ZVS) in the converters, while changing the relative phase shift can introduce reactive power into the system, resulting in increased losses in the coil and the converter. This article presents a novel Bd-IPT system that utilizes an integrated boost multilevel converter (IBMC) with a digitised modulation scheme. The primary objectives of the proposed Bd-IPT system are to maintain the desired power transfer, operate both the primary and secondary converters within the ZVS range, and achieve zero reactive power for a wide range of loading conditions. Additionally, the article compares the efficiency and cost of the proposed Bd-IPT system to a conventional IPT system.

articleTitle: Improved Cross-Helix Array with Efficient 360-Degree Steerable WPT for Solar Power Satellite
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Power Technology Conference and Expo (WPTCE)
abstract: In this paper, single and cross helix array structures, for solar power satellite WPT applications, have been simulated, with full wave simulations up to 200x100 unit cell (H x W = 6m x 6m) array size. Near field simulations computed the WPT power densities at distances up to 500 m from the array. The results presented, are the first validation that a large cross helix structure can provide enhanced, 360 degree steerable, WPT beamforming capabilities compared to a similarly sized single helix. Previous work has only validated single helix structures. As an example, a 100x100 single helix array with 5W per element was shown to produce a WPT power density of 93 W/m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> at 500m, whereas a 200x100 cross helix structure, with double the number of elements produced a power density of 315W/m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>, which is an almost fourfold increase compared to the single helix. This clearly shows the increased aperture to be providing additional beamforming as well as the two times power increase from doubling the number of elements.

articleTitle: Single-stage Wireless Charger with High Power Factor Input
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Power Technology Conference and Expo (WPTCE)
abstract: This paper proposes a single-stage Wireless-Power-Transfer (WPT) AC-DC converter with a high power factor. Compared to conventional two-stage WPT structures, the proposed single-stage wireless power transfer (SS-WPT) offers several advantages, including a low component count, interleaving effect, and soft switching commutation without electrolytic capacitors, leading to cost savings, high efficiency, and reliability. Unlike other existing SS-WPT systems that operate in discontinuous conduction mode (DCM), the proposed SS-WPT works in continuous conduction mode (CCM) with the help of interleaving, resulting in decreased core losses and input filter size. Additionally, a simple modulation technique is proposed with one control variable at the fixed switching frequency to regulate the output voltage and shape grid current simultaneously. Furthermore, the proposed modulation strategies also help reduce low-frequency ripples on the DC side without additional components, overcoming drawbacks of previous SS-WPT systems. A 500W SS-WPT laboratory prototype was built and tested to validate the effectiveness of the proposed integrated converter.

articleTitle: High Dynamic Range 920 MHz Band Low Power Rectenna With Low Threshold Voltage GaAs GADs
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Power Technology Conference and Expo (WPTCE)
abstract: In this paper, the 920 MHz band low power rectifiers with low threshold voltage GaAs gated anode diodes (GADs) are demonstrated for high dynamic range operation. The GaAs GAD has an advantage of controllability on threshold voltage. This enables low threshold voltage of GaAs GAD that is similar value as a Si SBD. In the developed 920 MHz band rectifiers that are the bridge type and the double voltage type, measured rectification efficiencies are higher than that with commercial based Si SBD. Measured sensitivities at output voltage of 0.3 V with open load are -26 dBm and -30 dBm, respectively. Furthermore, estimated maximum input powers are 11 dBm and 12 dBm, respectively. This indicates operation availability at near-field region to the transmitter. This clarifies extreme higher dynamic range of the developed GaAs rectifiers, compared with Si SBD or CMOS rectifiers in past works.

articleTitle: Thermal Modelling of IPT Coil Embedded in Resin for the Roadway
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Power Technology Conference and Expo (WPTCE)
abstract: This paper presents an investigation into the thermal behaviour of a copper coil embedded into a block of resin that is bound to the asphalt in the roadway. The roadway is made up of three layers of 50mm asphalt and the resin block surrounding the coil was placed within the surface layer. The thermal behaviour of the coil and the surrounding environment is presented when the coil is energised at 90A DC to be within the electromagnetic radiation limits. Based on the exerpimental results, simulations are conducted in ANSYS Maxwell and Icepak to predict the temperature rise using AC energisation at 85kHz. The coil is energised in the simulation with a range of currents to predict the thermal stress the resin block will withstand at steady-state conditions. The simulation findings predict the thermal behaviour of the resin block and the surrounding asphalt when the coil is transferring 10kW.

articleTitle: Input Voltage Range Optimization of a High Power Wireless Power Transfer System for Constant Power Output
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Power Technology Conference and Expo (WPTCE)
abstract: Designing wireless power transfer systems for high power energy transfer is challenging, especially when transferring constant power under misalignment and varying battery voltage. In systems with passive rectifiers, there are not many control parameters that can be adjusted to regulate the output. In order to maintain constant power under misalignment, common approaches normally require a large input voltage range. This results in either high cost for the active frontend or higher losses in the inverter due to increased hard switching. This work shows an optimization approach to transfer constant power in all alignment conditions by achieving the best possible efficiency while minimizing the input voltage range. An existing 50 kW wireless power transfer system is taken as a starting point for an optimization. The range minimization of the input voltage is achieved by modifying the compensation parameters of the LCC resonant network on the primary side. The optimization results are then shown and suitable solutions are compared to the standard resonant design.

articleTitle: Design of a Compact Rectangular Three-Phase Dynamic Wireless Power Transfer Receiver for Compatibility with a Preexisting Transmitter
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Power Technology Conference and Expo (WPTCE)
abstract: This paper details the design of a compact rectangular three-phase receiver to operate with a preexisting transmitter. Details are provided regarding the optimization-based design approach and the underpinning electromagnetic analysis. A selected optimized design is verified through an independent electromagnetic analysis, and the electrical performance is demonstrated through simulation within a full DWPT system. The overall design process demonstrates a means for independent vehicle manufacturers to design receiver systems tailored to their individual constraints while maintaining compatibility and interoperability with preexisting transmitter systems.

articleTitle: Design and demonstration of the volumetric resonator with uniform magnetic field distribution for wireless power transfer
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Power Technology Conference and Expo (WPTCE)
abstract: Here, we propose a volumetric resonator of two strongly coupled split loops to wirelessly charge devices within the internal volume. The resonator possesses a unique feature: the ability to generate an almost uniform magnetic field with 96% uniformity within the volume. This uniformity enables energy transfer to the receiver with fixed efficiency, regardless of the receiver’s location inside the resonator. Numerical and experimental calculations have demonstrated that the wireless power transfer efficiency can reach up to 30%, making the power transmission efficiency almost independent of the receiver’s location within the entire internal volume of the resonator. This solution is designed for discreet embedding in small furniture modules or standard-shaped living spaces, allowing people to charge their devices without sacrificing mobility.

articleTitle: Analysis of Near-Field Magnetic Flux in the Three-Dimensional Wireless Power Transmitter
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Power Technology Conference and Expo (WPTCE)
abstract: This paper presents the analysis of the near-field magnetic flux in a three-dimensional wireless power transmitter. The three-dimensional wireless power transmitter is constructed based on the concept of Helmholtz coil, which was originally invented for generating a constant static magnetic field. In recent years, this concept has been applied to wireless power transfer, enabling omnidirectional wireless charging. To facilitate the analysis and implementation of such three-dimensional wireless power transmitters, we conducted an analysis on their magnetic field distribution. In this study, we first present the theoretical calculation results. Additionally, we provide finite element simulation results and experimental data to verify the analysis. Moreover, we incorporate the magnetic flux modulation technique to the wireless power transmitter. By combining the evenly distributed magnetic flux and this modulation technique, a consistent magnetic flux linkage on the receiver coil is achieved.

articleTitle: A scalable wireless power transmission system and its target tracking beaming using a direction of arrival estimator
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Power Technology Conference and Expo (WPTCE)
abstract: An active 5.8 GHz wireless power transmission (WPT) system based on scalable transmission and reception modules is developed. The transmitter is a planar active phased array system powered by gallium-nitride class-F power amplifiers and consists of 24 microwave power transfer (MPT) modules integrated with a subarray antenna. Each of the MPT modules can work alone as well as be driven with other modules and also be expanded further. The power receiving system comprises 128 rectenna modules whose DC outputs are combined in parallel. The placement can be modified or extended more to correspond to the width and shape of the incoming beam. A hardware configuration for a concise direction of arrival (DOA) estimation system, composed of a multi-channel switch, a phase modulator, and a power combiner, is also proposed. The azimuth and elevation direction are derived from the method of element electric-field vector by measuring only the amplitudes of a combined field vector. The proposed DOA estimation system and a pilot signal transmitter of 2.45 GHz were installed on the WPT system, and an experiment tracking a target 50 m away was conducted. It could be visually confirmed that the real-time tracking transmission operates properly while maintaining a pencil beam of 1.8 ° width.

articleTitle: Power Stabilization of Dynamic Wireless Power Transfer System with Grid-connected Photovoltaic and DC Bus Voltage Control
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Power Technology Conference and Expo (WPTCE)
abstract: Dynamic Wireless Power Transfer (DWPT), which has been attracting attention in recent years, is a system that solves the problems of Electric Vehicles (EVs), such as long charging times and short cruising ranges. This study proposes a system for local production and local consumption of electricity by using grid-connected photovoltaic (PV) as an energy source for DWPT. When the PV is generating excess power compared to the electricity demand, the power is returned to the grid. When the PV is not generating enough power, the grid subsidizes the shortage. In this way, the DCbus voltage can be maintained at a constant level, enabling a stable supply of power to the EV on the demand side. The effectiveness of the proposed system was verified using circuit analysis software (MATLAB/Simulink), which enables stable DWPT while performing maximum power point tracking (MPPT) control of the PV panels and DCbus voltage control using a Dual Active Bridge (DAB) converter connected to the Grid side. The results show that the DCbus voltage can be controlled within plus or minus 1 percent of the target value regardless of the fluctuating PV and the coupling coefficient between the transmission and receiving coils, and the power conversion efficiency of the DWPT was up to 70 percent. Thus, the proposed system was found to be effective and feasible.

articleTitle: Enhancing RF Energy Harvesting and Wireless Power Transfer with GAN-Optimized 3D Quasi-Yagi Antenna
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Power Technology Conference and Expo (WPTCE)
abstract: Radio Frequency Energy Harvesting (RFEH) and Wireless Power Transfer (WPT) are increasingly popular for powering low-power devices, with the design of receiving antennas being a key factor. This paper presents a cube-shaped 3D antenna, innovatively derived from the quasi-Yagi antenna (QYA) design and optimized for operation at 915 MHz. Unlike traditional 2D and directional antennas, this 3D design offers multidirectional reception, which is crucial for efficiently harvesting varying levels of dedicated and ambient energy. Using CST Studio tools for simulation, the antenna, based on an optimized 2D QYA model (Type D with 6.24 dBi gain and 43.87 dB return loss), achieved a high gain of 11.43 dBi, a return loss of 45.61 dB, and a bandwidth of 25 MHz, as verified by the N9912A FieldFox HandHeld RF Analyzer and ME1310 Antenna Training Kit (3D) Dream Catcher. Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) were utilized for data augmentation and optimization, reducing the reliance on extensive data collection. Additionally, the integration of this 3D antenna with an impedance-matching network and subsequent experimental harvesting with a 1.5 kΩ resistor demonstrate its practicality. We thus propose a versatile and efficient RFEH solution suitable for a range of RF sources and applications.

articleTitle: MPPT-Controlled Adaptive Reconfigurable 5.8GHz RF Energy Harvesting Front-End in 65nm CMOS
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Power Technology Conference and Expo (WPTCE)
abstract: The range of input power levels that allow a RF energy harvester to produce an output level required to power a WSN node is limited. The limitation is caused by the losses arising from the static configuration of the RF energy harvester that is not ideal for a wide range of input power levels expected from RF energy sources. A dynamic RF energy harvester where both the matching network and rectifier are reconfigurable to adapt to the input power level improves the sensitivity and provides voltage regulation, extending the operating range. To implement this, the number of stages in the rectifier cascade and the input impedance produced by the matching network are modified. Several configurations could produce the required output, but the most efficient configuration for different input power levels is chosen using a Maximum Power Point Tracking (MPPT) mechanism to maximize the power harvested from RF sources. Simulation results for a design implemented in 65nm CMOS process show an improvement of around 17dB in dynamic range and up to 20% in efficiency for a dynamic RF energy harvester implementing MPPT compared to a static RF energy harvester in producing a 1V output using a 5.8GHz input. Silicon test results show that the performance of the dynamic rectifier is close to simulated results at around -8dBm, 5.8GHz RF input while providing a form of voltage regulation at high power input that increases dynamic range and removing the need for large voltage limiter circuits.

articleTitle: Listening to the Whispers: Enhanced SWIPT Wake-Up Receiver for IoT Sensors
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Power Technology Conference and Expo (WPTCE)
abstract: To address the challenges of energy constraints in Wireless Sensor Networks and Internet of Things devices, this study presents an enhanced wake-up receiver for Simultaneous Wireless Information and Power Transfer applications. The proposed design incorporates a passive 2 × 2 Multiple-Input Multiple-Output antenna configuration, which enhances the sensitivity and reliability of detecting wake-up signals under diverse environmental conditions. The architecture also includes a two-stage rectifier and an operational amplifier to efficiently harvest energy from radio-frequency signals. An important breakthrough is the integration of backscattering technology, which allows the wake-up receiver to support battery-less operations in Internet of Things networks. This effectively minimizes energy consumption and prolongs the lifespan of the Internet of Things devices. The double function of the receiver to activate sensor nodes and transmit data through radio frequency signals provides a practical and environmentally friendly solution for the Internet of Things.

Author Keywords: Simultaneous Wireless Information and Power Transfer (SWIPT)

articleTitle: High-Frequency Load-Independent Wireless Power Charging System
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Power Technology Conference and Expo (WPTCE)
abstract: This paper proposes a load-independent high-frequency wireless power transfer (WPT) system. The proposed system achieves mode switching between constant current (CC) and constant voltage (CV) output modes, which can be applied to rechargeable batteries. In the proposed system, a single switch component is added on the receiver side to change the topology of the compensation circuit. As a result, the switching between CC and CV modes is accomplished on the receiver side, which means wireless communication about the load-information feedback from the receiver to the transmitter becomes unnecessary. By achieving zero-voltage switching (ZVS) in both CC and CV modes through the load-independent operation, the proposed system achieves high power-delivery efficiency even at high frequencies. Therefore, the proposed WPT system contributes to cost reduction, system simplification, and circuit downsizing. The experimental results agreed with the analytical predictions quantitatively, which verified the effectiveness of the proposed circuits.

articleTitle: Influence of Salinity on Contactless Power Transmission System in Seawater
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Power Technology Conference and Expo (WPTCE)
abstract: This paper describes the influence of salinity on a contactless power transmission system in seawater. The transmission efficiency, power, and total power loss are measured in changing salinity through experiments. In order to investigate these factors, magnetic flux density, the number of chain fluxes, main flux, and leakage flux have been measured by magnetic field analysis with JMAG. In this paper, the leakage flux and transmission system of salinity are investigated from the results of simulation and experiments. It is found that the increased salinity causes the decrease in power efficiency.

articleTitle: A Novel Active Inductive Clamping Class E Topology and Its Design Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Power Technology Conference and Expo (WPTCE)
abstract: Wireless power transfer (WPT) realizes nonconductor contact power transmission with the advantages of plug-free and high spatial freedom by means of electromagnetic field, mechanical wave, acoustic wave, etc. The development of WPT cannot be achieved without the advancement of high frequency power amplifiers. Class E ZVS inverters are the most efficient inverters so far, with the advantages of high-power density, simple circuit topology and low electromagnetic interference. However, WPT is an application with dramatically load variations for power amplifiers, which is really unfriendly to class E inverters. This article develops the explicit design of active inductive clamping class E inverter (AICCEI) with wide load range of zero-voltage switching (ZVS) to improve the robustness of WPT system against the variations of final load and coil-coupling. Two kinds of AICCEI design strategies are derived with the features of 50% duty cycle and non-50% duty cycle and the steady-state behavior are demonstrated. The design of bi-direction clamping source is critical to the operation of AICCEI, and the keys to design will also be presented in this paper. The steady-state behavior and transient response of AICCEI have been tested. The efficiency of the 40W AICCEI is up to 94.2% at 6.78MHz with nominal operation condition. The ZVS operation is achieved when the equivalent resistance of the capacitive load greater than the rated value in the experimental. With the active clamping source, the overshoot voltage of MOSFET is reduced from 145V to 87.6V when the load of AICCEI is cut.

articleTitle: Series Series Compensation Topology for Load Independent Current and Voltage Output in Wireless Power Transfer System
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Power Technology Conference and Expo (WPTCE)
abstract: This article addresses the need for an efficient and compact wireless power transfer (WPT) system for Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs), focusing on constant current-constant voltage (CC-CV) output for secure Li-ion battery charging. The work proposes a straightforward WPT with a series-series compensation topology to achieve the desired CC-CV output, highlighting load variations, soft switching, and efficiency. The simulations indicate that circular coils in the system offer higher coupling coefficients. Furthermore, inverter switches are designed for both zero voltage switching (ZVS) and zero current switching (ZCS) at the respective turn-ON and turn-OFF conditions in CC charging, while only ZVS at turn-ON condition in CV charging, ensuring high efficiency. A 69 W prototype, with coupling coefficient (k = 0.2), operating frquency at 77.3 kHz in CC mode and 86.5 kHz in CV mode, validates the proposed system.

articleTitle: An Ambient Energy Harvesting Interface for Battery-Free Wireless Sensor Nodes
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Power Technology Conference and Expo (WPTCE)
abstract: This paper presents a low-quiescent-power battery-free energy harvesting interface for micro-watt to milli-watt applications with a single-inductor dual-input dual-output (SIDIDO) buck-boost converter. The system contains one renewable source input, one regulated output and one bidirectional energy transfer node with a storage capacitor for storage and reuse the energy. To achieve high power conversion efficiency (PCE) with micro-watt input power, we embedded dynamic-power-gating under-voltage lockout (DPG-UVLO) circuit, dynamic-voltage-feedback (DVFB) and pulse-frequency modulation (PFM) control to reduce quiescent power. The measurement quiescent power is 1.9 µW and the peak PCE is 86.4%.

articleTitle: Room-Sized Helmholtz-Type Resonator for Ubiquitous Wireless Power Transfer
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Power Technology Conference and Expo (WPTCE)
abstract: This study introduces a Helmholtz-type resonator for wireless charging low-power devices in a room-scale environment. A unique feature of this resonator is a uniformly magnetic field distribution, reaching 91.1% coverage within 1/4 of the resonator’s internal volume. This maintenance of high magnetic field uniformity contributes to a stable power transfer efficiency (PTE) as observed in simulations, exhibiting only minor fluctuations within the range of 5.6% to 8.3%. Our experimental investigation successfully demonstrated the wireless charging of various devices, including a fan, smartphone, nightlight, and lamp, achieving an overall PTE of 12%. Furthermore, our findings indicated that the specific absorption rate values remained below the stipulated safety thresholds regarding the safety regulations outlined in the IEEE Std C95.1™-2019. The proposed volumetric resonator presented in this study represents a significant advancement, as it promises to elevate the concept of smart home technologies, enabling multiple individuals to access a charging infrastructure for their electronic devices without sacrificing mobility. Additionally, this innovation offers a convenient solution for integrating electrical devices within room interiors.

articleTitle: Improving the Effective Range of a Through the Soil Long Range Wireless Power Transfer System Using a Marx Inverter Topology
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Power Technology Conference and Expo (WPTCE)
abstract: With the growing research into Through the Soil wireless power transfer systems, power supply design research is necessary for determining a suitable topology capable of supplying high current density. A modified Marx inverter is chosen to complete this task due to the extremely high voltages produced. The presented analysis shows that TTS system performance metrics greatly improve with increased current density and high operating frequency. Finally, the inverter is used to operate a Through the Soil wireless power transfer system and its performance is assessed.

articleTitle: Study of High Efficiency Thin Barrier AlGaN/GaN Schottky Barrier Diodes and Rectifiers
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Power Technology Conference and Expo (WPTCE)
abstract: Rectifiers performance affects the overall efficiency of microwave wireless power transfer systems. The performance of the rectifier device (usually used Schottky diode) determines the upper limit of the rectifier. In order to improve the efficiency and input power of the rectifier, we designed and prepared thin barrier AlGaN/GaN heterojunction rectifier devices. The device achieved 80% conversion efficiency and operates at 5.8 GHz with maximum input power of 28.5 dBm.

articleTitle: A Solenoid Magnetic Coupler With a Rotating Magnetic Field for UAVs Wireless Charging
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Power Technology Conference and Expo (WPTCE)
abstract: This paper proposes a solenoid magnetic coupler for unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) wireless charging, which can significantly reduce leakage magnetic flux interference on UAV equipment. The transmitter is composed of three-phase solenoid coils, it mainly generates horizontal magnetic flux while the vertical magnetic flux is very weak, resulting in low leakage magnetic flux interference. The receiver consists of two solenoid coils wound at the landing gear of the UAV, which is compact, lightweight, and conformal. Besides, it will not increase additional installation space or increase wind drag. A rotating magnetic field is generated under excitation currents phase difference of 120°, which ensures power transmission stability regardless of the UAV's angle and position. The simulation results show that the received power maintains at 75 W-105 W under any receiver angle or position, which indicates that the proposed system has good rotational and positional misalignment tolerance.

articleTitle: Optimal Design of Decoupling Networks to Improve MIMO Microwave Wireless Power Transfer
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Power Technology Conference and Expo (WPTCE)
abstract: Long range wireless power transfer (WPT) is envisioned to employ multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) systems to control the current distribution on a large antenna, allowing for a more accurate beam-forming. Presence of multiple antenna elements creates mutual coupling between them which reduces the WPT efficiency. To improve this, a decoupling network (DN) can be used in a similar way that impedance matching networks are used in single-input single-output (SISO) WPT systems. The design method of a DN has been established by many different works for a MIMO antenna in communication systems, but WPT systems exhibit a loading effect that is not considered in these works. Therefore, the resulting DN from them can only achieve suboptimal efficiency in WPT. In this paper, we present an algorithm to simultaneously synthesize a DN for both the generator antenna array and the receiver antenna array which considers the loading effect problem. Through a co-simulation of an electromagnetic simulator and a circuit simulator, we demonstrate how the proposed DN design algorithm outperforms the analytic DN design for communication antennas.

articleTitle: The Mitigation of Received Power Variation from Same-Frequency Sources by Binary Phase Shift Keying Modulation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Power Technology Conference and Expo (WPTCE)
abstract: In a two-transmitter array with the same frequency sources, if one transmitter uses BPSK modulation with an equal duration of 0º and 180º states, the average received power is the power sum from two transmitters instead of the voltage vector sum of the signals from two sources. As interference between two received signals is mitigated, stable received power can be achieved over different receiver locations. The stable received power is observed over different locations in the experiment and agrees well with the calculation. This modulation has the potential to realize simultaneous wireless information and power transfer (SWIPT) with smaller received power variation over different receiver locations.

articleTitle: Optimized Design and Performance Analysis of 13.56 MHz Printed-Circuit-Board Resonators for Efficient Wireless Power Transfer
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Power Technology Conference and Expo (WPTCE)
abstract: This paper presents a novel design method for Printed-Circuit-Board (PCB) resonators consisting of two PCBs with an airgap. The resonators are accurately modeled using a third-order circuit and optimized for a specific target frequency of 13.56MHz. Furthermore, the coupling coefficient of the coupled coils formed by two resonators at different distances is rigorously analyzed and validated using the Hurley-Duffy Equation. The impedance characteristics of both the single resonator and the coupled coils are experimentally verified. A 48W experimental result demonstrates a transmission efficiency of 97.41% at 13.2 MHz for the designed coils.

articleTitle: A 6-Element Helical Retrodirective Array for High Power Wireless Power Transmission
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Power Technology Conference and Expo (WPTCE)
abstract: In this paper we provide the test results of a 6-element, high power, phased array antenna used for radiative wireless power transmission. A retrodirective approach is used to target the power transmission in a desired direction. The frequency used for the power transmission is 2.496GHz which lies in the 2.4-2.5GHz ISM frequency band. We used a 6 element array of helical antennas to transmit the electromagnetic power. Retrodirective operation was practically validated for the 6 element array with total transmit power of 60W (10W per element) at up to 84% drain efficiency at the transmit power amplifiers. The tests have been carried out in the Queen’s University Belfast anechoic chamber at the Centre of Wireless Innovation (CWI).

articleTitle: Development of Experimental System for Dynamic Wireless Power Transfer Utilizing Circular Motion
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Power Technology Conference and Expo (WPTCE)
abstract: There is a requirement to develop a simplified experimental system which can simulate DWPT for EVs. This paper elucidates the detailed construction method for the DWPT system utilizing circular motion. In the experiments, it demonstrates the possibility of transmitting 3 kW of power at a speed equivalent to 17 km/h in linear motion, allowing experiments to be conducted at a power transmission scale close to actual DWPT.

articleTitle: LUT-Based Transmit Mode Calibration Complexity Reduction Method for Wireless Power Transfer
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Power Technology Conference and Expo (WPTCE)
abstract: This paper introduces a calibration method for transmitter arrays for the power transmit mode in wireless power transfer (WPT) systems. Focusing on the challenges posed by non-uniform power distribution in large array antenna systems, we propose a technique adaptable to various power distribution designs. Our method also simplifies the calibration process, making it feasible for real-world applications with large array antennas. The paper validates our methodology, from the hardware system to experimental results, demonstrating the effectiveness of our approach by transmitting CVX optimized radiation patterns. The receiver array achieved received RF power of 3.57 Watts at 0.5 meters.

articleTitle: Wireless Power Transmission for Left Ventricular Assist Devices: Advancements, Challenges, and Future Directions
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Power Technology Conference and Expo (WPTCE)
abstract: This paper discusses the state of the art of applying wireless power transfer (WPT) to power a left ventricular assist device (LVAD) which is an implanted heart pump to support failing hearts of heart failure patients. Starting from the historical background of LVAD therapy and systems, the WPT applications proposed in the last two decades to eliminate the driveline infection (DLI) are presented highlighting differences in proposed solutions and technological advances. Finally, future directions are presented underlining that the use of LVAD as destination therapy instead of "bridge-to-transplant" therapy is very likely thanks to WPT technology.

articleTitle: An Integrated Boost Multilevel Converter using Si and SiC switches for Inductive Power Transfer Application
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Power Technology Conference and Expo (WPTCE)
abstract: Misalignment between the transmitter and receiver coils in an Inductive Power Transfer (IPT) degrades the efficiency and reduces the power transfer to the Electric Vehicle (EV). This issue is further aggravated by variations in the battery voltage, making it challenging to design a power converter for such applications. The challenge is typically overcome either by employing superior SiC MOSFETs with pre-regulation, which are expensive, or by utilizing complex control and compensation schemes. A low-voltage Si MOSFET based Integrated Boost Multilevel Converter (IBMC) topology has been proposed as a solution, but the requirement for 12 submodules (SMs) impacts the efficiency and also significantly increases costs. This article enhances the IBMC topology by introducing a new configuration that utilizes both Si and SiC MOSFETs to reduce the switch count, thereby decreasing the cost and losses of the system. Additionally, the work extends the digitized modulation scheme proposed for an IBMC to enhance the number of digitized states with fewer submodules, facilitating operation over a wide Zero Voltage Switching (ZVS) range

articleTitle: Integrated Shielding and Energy Harvesting by an Optimized Near-field Metamaterial-based System
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Power Technology Conference and Expo (WPTCE)
abstract: Combined near-field shielding and energy harvesting using a magnetic metamaterial for low-frequency (85 kHz) inductive wireless power transfer (WPT) system is proposed. The paper discusses the potential applications of this technology, along with illustrating the key components and design considerations for energy harvesting through metamaterial-based shields. A reference case study is considered, and a constrained multi-objective optimisation is performed for the tuning of the metamaterial-based energy-harvesting system.

articleTitle: Miniature Wireless Power Transfer System for Charging Vertically Oriented Receivers
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Power Technology Conference and Expo (WPTCE)
abstract: Development of compact wireless power transfer (WPT) systems for charging miniature randomly oriented electronic devices is quite a challenge. Traditionally, WPT systems based on resonant magnetic coupling utilize face-to-face aligned transmitter and receiver coils providing sufficient efficiency at relatively large distances. However, with the presence of angular receiver misalignment in a such system, the mutual coupling decreases resulting in a low power transfer efficiency. Here we develop a compact WPT system for wireless charging of miniature receivers vertically oriented with respect to the transmitter. As a transmitter, we employ a butterfly coil that provides a strong tangential component of the magnetic field. Thus, a vertically oriented receiver located in the magnetic field can be charged wirelessly. We perform numerical and experimental studies of the WPT system’s power transfer efficiency as a function of the distance between the transmitter and the receiver. The misalignment and rotation dependencies of power transfer efficiency are also experimentally studied. We demonstrate the power transfer efficiency of 60 % within transfer distance of 4 mm for a vertically oriented receiver with an overall dimension of 20 mm ×14 mm at the frequency of 6.78 MHz.

articleTitle: Mitigation of Magnetic Fields in Dynamic Wireless Power Transfer Systems through Passive Compensation Loops
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Power Technology Conference and Expo (WPTCE)
abstract: This paper deals with the mitigation of magnetic field emissions produced by dynamic wireless power transfer (DWPT) systems. Passive compensation loops are proposed as an effective mitigation technique in the case of a DWPT system having the configuration used in the European Fabric project, for which the field levels do not greatly exceed the reference levels (RLs) of the ICNIRP 2010 guidelines. The proposed solution based on passive compensation loops is simple, economical, and robust. However, as the DWPT coils are not immune to external fields such as those produced by the passive compensation circuits themselves, particular attention must be paid in their design. Finally, the investigation performed by numerical simulations will show that the proposed configuration of a DWPT system with compensation loops complies with the ICNIRP RLs.

articleTitle: Discrete-Time Modeling for IPT Systems with Constant Voltage Load
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Power Technology Conference and Expo (WPTCE)
abstract: Inductive power transfer (IPT) technology has attracted more attention due to its convenience and safety. The mathematical model is an effective tool for analyzing and optimizing the performance of IPT systems. Many previous articles on modeling equate the load to a pure resistor, which can simplify the modeling process. However, this assumption is not reliable for the battery load. In this paper, the discrete-time model is derived for the IPT system with a constant voltage load. Four switching modes are defined in each cycle according to the switching states of the inverter and rectifier, the state equations are derived based on the equivalent circuit, and the discrete-time model is solved by iteration. Finally, simulations and experiments are both conducted to verify the accuracy of the established model.

articleTitle: Study on Estimating the Full Mutual Inductance Information in Multi-Receiver Wireless Power Transfer Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Power Technology Conference and Expo (WPTCE)
abstract: To operate stably and optimally a multi-receiver wireless power transfer (WPT) system, the full mutual inductance information including cross couplings is required. However, little research has been developed to estimate the full mutual inductance information of a multi-receiver WPT system. This study proposes a two-stage approach for estimating the full mutual inductance information of a multi-receiver WPT system. At the first stage, the mutual inductance between the transmitter and each receiver is calculated. Then, at the second stage, the mutual inductance (i.e., cross coupling) between two receivers is sequentially estimated. Through experimental results, the proposed method demonstrates that it can precisely estimate the full mutual inductance information of a multi-receiver WPT system.

articleTitle: Power Injection Compensation for M-PSK Modulation Achieving SWPDT in Medical Implants
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Power Technology Conference and Expo (WPTCE)
abstract: Reliable communication and robust power supply are critical requirements for medical implants. However, the achievable data rates are constrained by the large time constant due to the system's high quality (Q) factor. Additionally, achieving high data rates through PSK modulation can significantly reduce the average transfer power to the implant during phase shifts. This paper introduces M-PSK modulation and power injection compensation to enhance data rates and ensure reliable power transfer during communication. A lead-lag phase detector is implemented to demodulate the received signal. In a benchtop experiment, the IPT system (Qp=78.4) transmitted a 32-bit data sequence at 222kbps at 6.667MHz with zero error. The compensation improves the average load power from 79.7% to 101.2% of the unmodulated value.

articleTitle: Position and Attitude Error Forecasting Technology of Microwave Power Transmitting Arrays for Space Solar Power Station
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Power Technology Conference and Expo (WPTCE)
abstract: Microwave power transmission (MPT) in the space environment is based on the ideal profile of power transmitting array, without considering the influence of spatial complexity factors (solar pressure, gravity gradient, attitude orbit coupling, etc.) on the position and attitude of structural modules in microwave power transmitting array, especially on ultra large-scale antenna arrays, which require high structural rigidity and attitude control of antenna modules. In this paper, we propose a microwave power transmission antenna position and attitude error prediction technology based on Spatial- temporal Series Forecasting technology. Multiple cycles and a large number of images can be captured through a monocular camera to predict the structural modules of the transmitting sub-array that are about to be influenced by position and attitude errors. Predicting the position and attitude errors of structural modules assist in retro-directive beam steering. This method theoretically verifies the ability to correct the positional deviations of the structural modules in microwave power transmitting array, providing advance technical support for the development and construction of space solar power stations in the second and third stages in the future.

articleTitle: Optical Wireless Power Transfer Network System for Multiple AE Sensors
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Power Technology Conference and Expo (WPTCE)
abstract: We present our recent research on an OWPT network system for multiple acoustic emission (AE) sensors using 808 nm laser diodes (LDs) and silicon-based photovoltaic (PV) cells. A Bluetooth network was used for data and control communication between the sensors and control PC, and a galvanometer was used to control the direction of the laser beam and supply power to each AE sensor module. Based on the results of this study, a GaAs-based PV cell was introduced as the optimal PV cell for the OWPT network system for multiple AE sensors, and the design of the PV cell epi-structure and top electrode pattern was carried out.

articleTitle: Energy Harvesting from AM Broadcasting Radio Waves with High-Q Ferrite Rod Antenna and High-Efficiency Rectifier Designed Using Simple Equation-Based Model
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Power Technology Conference and Expo (WPTCE)
abstract: The energy harvesting system, which consists of a high-Q ferrite rod antenna and a high-efficiency rectifier, was developed to efficiently harvest power from AM broadcasting radio waves. The rectifier and its impedance matching to the antenna were optimally designed using a newly proposed simple equation-based rectifier model. The system was tested in the field and demonstrated excellent performance, harvesting 1.25 μW of DC power at a distance of 6.35 km from an AM radio station transmitting 500 kW of radio waves at 774 kHz.

articleTitle: Optimum Feeding Strategy for Agile Wireless Powering by Large, High-Directivity Time-Modulated Arrays
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Power Technology Conference and Expo (WPTCE)
abstract: Aim of the paper is to show a practical solution to the problem of designing bi-dimensional planar time-modulated arrays (TMAs) with a high number of radiating elements to be exploited in precise wireless power transfer applications. Despite being a widely discussed issue, it is typically faced from a purely theoretical point of view. The described and realized radial arrangement operating at 2.45 GHz not only exploits the benefits of the circular symmetry, but also allows, for the first time, an easy and feasible control of the time-modulated mechanism through the reduction of the driving switches number. Despite this, the almost real-time reconfiguration of the radial TMA is also validated by numerical optimization.

articleTitle: Cryogenic Inductive Power Transfer System
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Power Technology Conference and Expo (WPTCE)
abstract: This paper presents a demonstration inductive power transfer system operating at 77 K, transferring 17 W over a 5 mm air gap. Such a system could have applications in high-temperature superconducting magnets, satellites and asteroid mining. A GaN HEMT full bridge inverter is used with careful selection of the tuning components to reduce mis-tuning effects with temperature variation. The key equations, magnetic coupler design, tuning topology and component selection are presented, and the system is simulated, constructed, and validated in the laboratory. The presented methodology can be modified for contact-less power delivery in satellite applications or for supporting HTS magnets in space or terrestrial scenarios.

articleTitle: Theoretical Analysis of Litz-Wire DD Coil for Wireless Power Transfer System
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Power Technology Conference and Expo (WPTCE)
abstract: Coupler design becomes a key factor affecting efficiency and practicality in the rapidly evolving field of wireless power transfer systems, especially in the field of electric vehicle charging. The design of different coupler systems will have different self-inductance, mutual inductance and AC resistance, which will affect the energy transmission efficiency and transmission capacity of the system. However, the coupler design purely relying on finite element analysis (FEA) software is time-consuming. In this paper, the inductance of the DD planar coil is calculated using the theoretical calculation method, and the wire spacing and number of turns at different positions of the DD coil are changed respectively when other coil parameters are unchanged, and the inductance of the DD coil under different parameters is calculated and the simulation under different parameters is performed to obtain the simulation value of the DD coil inductance. By comparing the calculated inductance value of DD coil with the simulation value, the accuracy of the theoretical calculation method of DD coil inductance in this paper is obtained, and certain guidance is provided for the design and simulation of DD coil, avoiding the workload caused by the repeated design of coil model caused by the cumbersome change of simulation model parameters.

articleTitle: Thermal Modelling of Resonant Capacitor Boards for Inductive Power Transfer Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Power Technology Conference and Expo (WPTCE)
abstract: Resonant capacitor boards are used in compensation networks for inductive power transfer (IPT) systems. IPT systems typically use class 1 multilayer ceramic capacitors (MLCC) due to their high stability and relatively low losses. However, the losses of class 1 MLCCs are still a concern at high power levels and limit the power density of IPT systems due to thermal constraints. This paper characterizes the losses of a commercially available class 1 MLCC (TDK C0G) using calorimetric methods and predicts the temperature rise of resonant capacitor boards using computational fluid dynamics (CFD) simulations. The losses of the C0G capacitors used in the resonant capacitor boards were measured to be almost constant over a 60 °C temperature range. Steady-state simulations matched within 10.5%, and transient results were within 16.3%.

articleTitle: Nanocrystalline Core Loss in High Power IPT Systems for EV Charging Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Power Technology Conference and Expo (WPTCE)
abstract: Mn-Zn ferrite is commonly used in inductive power transfer (IPT) systems to enhance magnetic coupling and reduce flux leakage. However, ferrite is not ideal for high power transfer due to the large volume of material needed for its low saturation flux density, brittleness, and high core loss leading to thermal issues. Nanocrystalline alloys are potential alternatives to replace ferrite in IPT pads to improve magnetic performance. This paper analyses the core loss and equivalent series resistance (ESR) of ferrite and nanocrystalline cores in high-power IPT pads based on the measurement of magnetic properties using the partial cancellation method. The experimental findings show that the ESR of IPT pads using nanocrystalline cores decreases with higher excitation current in the pads, contrary to the typical behaviour of IPT pads using ferrite.

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis and Design of Class-E Inductive and Capacitive Power Transfer Systems for Non-Mating Connectors
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Power Technology Conference and Expo (WPTCE)
abstract: In this paper, a 13.56-MHz inductive power transfer (IPT) system and a 13.56-MHz capacitive power transfer (CPT) system are designed and compared for non-mating connector (NMC) applications. Circuits designs are based on a Class-E inverter to improve the performances with zero voltage switching (ZVS). Circuits are designed from the parameters of each coupler. Both systems performances are simulated and measured on fabricated prototypes: for 20 V input, the IPT system, outputting 43.3 W for 78.4 % of efficiency, outperformed the proposed CPT system, which outputs 12.3W for 65.8 % of efficiency.

articleTitle: Development of Omnidirectional Wireless Power Transfer based on Axial Magnetic Quadrupole Mode of Dielectric Resonator
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Power Technology Conference and Expo (WPTCE)
abstract: An efficient omnidirectional wireless power transfer (WPT) of portable devices is in high demand. It can find a wide application to charge portable devices regarding their orientation and location with respect to a WPT system transmitter. To reach this goal one needs to design a transmitter with an omnidirectional magnetic field distribution. In this paper, we propose and develop an omnidirectional magnetic resonant WPT system based on a transmitter realized as a dielectric hollow cylinder resonator with ultra-high permittivity and low loss, operating on axial magnetic quadrupole mode. The results of numerical investigations and proof-of-the-concept experiments are demonstrated and discussed. The omnidirectional WPT system efficiency of 90 % is achieved at the operational frequency of 154 MHz for the transfer distance of 3 cm, regardless of several receivers angular positions.

articleTitle: Thermal Analysis of the Encapsulation of Resonance Circuit Modules for the Paving Into Electric Road Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Power Technology Conference and Expo (WPTCE)
abstract: Electric Road Systems (ERS) for electric vehicles seem to be a promising solution to increase the range of electric vehicles without having to use larger batteries. Therefore, the resonance circuits have to be deployed into the roadways very precise to ensure best transmission efficiency and no breakdowns due to insufficient installation. Beside the manufacturing and deployment processes, the product properties have to be adapted to the requirements of road construction technologies. The main objective of this paper is to use simulation results and practical validation of materials and systems to determine the thermal requirements of resonant coil circuits for ERS. From the construction technologies of asphalt roads as well as the operation of electric road systems, the resulting material requirements for the encapsulation are determined. By characterization of different insulation materials, simulation models on the thermal impact of the system components are derived. The models are validated through practical test setups. The results provide knowledge that can be used to optimize the product design to different use cases in operation as well as construction.

articleTitle: Design Method of High Efficiency Rectenna for Microwave Power Transmission
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Power Technology Conference and Expo (WPTCE)
abstract: A rectenna is an essential component of a microwave power transmission system. For highly efficient rectenna design, extracting the diode’s maximum rectification efficiency is crucial. This study proposes the calculation method of the theoretical efficiency of the diode and summarizes how to design a rectenna. In this paper, we calculated the theoretical efficiency of a GaAs Schottky barrier diode. The calculation result shows that the maximum rectification efficiency reaches 96.4% with the fundamental frequency of 920 MHz, the input power of 30.4 dBm, and the load resistance of 800 Ω, respectively.

articleTitle: Power Efficient Simultaneous Wireless Information Transception and Power Reception Through an Isolation Barrier
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Power Technology Conference and Expo (WPTCE)
abstract: We present a power efficient structure for simultaneous wireless information transception and power reception through an isolation barrier. The structure utilises a binary frequency shift keying (BFSK) communication scheme for efficient power and information reception and on-off-keying (OOK) harmonic backscattering for information transmission. The structure achieves an overall system efficiency above 55 % from 20 dBm to 26 dBm input power while receiving a BFSK signal with up to 40 MSym and backscattering a 100 kHz PWM signal.

Author Keywords: simultaneous wireless information and power transfer (SWIPT)

articleTitle: Design of a Capacitive Power Transfer System with Tolerance of Large Coupling Variations
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Power Technology Conference and Expo (WPTCE)
abstract: This paper presents a new design methodology for capacitive power transfer (CPT) systems aimed at enhancing insensitivity to coupling variations. The designed CPT system maintains quasi-constant output power regardless of large coupling variations caused by misalignment. Its compensation network is designed to generate a constant current source. Design equations are derived for determining circuit parameters. The conditions and allowable range of the coupling variations are specified. Simulations and experimental results have demonstrated the validity of the proposed design method. A prototype CPT system has been built, capable of delivering up to 10W output power, with coupling changing from good alignment to 70mm longitudinal deviation.

articleTitle: User-Defined Power Distribution for Capacitive Wireless Power Transfer With Multiple Receivers
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Power Technology Conference and Expo (WPTCE)
abstract: Capacitive power transfer allows for wireless charging of multiple devices at once. In a typical system, the amount of power delivered to the different devices is determined by their position and distance to the transmitter. However, it can be beneficial to prioritize the charging of the devices. For example, if a critical device has a low battery status, the system should be able to prioritize the charging of this specific receiver above other nearly fully charged devices, even if the position or distance of this receiver is not optimal. In this work, we present a methodology to realize a user-defined power distribution to an arbitrary number of receivers within a capacitive wireless power transfer system. It applies admittance inverters in each receiver to regulate the power delivery. The results are numerically validated in the simulation program LT Spice on an illustrative system.

articleTitle: A Wideband Tuning Method for Extended Operating Frequency Range of Wireless Power Receiver
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Power Technology Conference and Expo (WPTCE)
abstract: This paper proposes a wideband tuning method for extended operating frequency range of an inductive power transfer (IPT) receiver by exploiting the variable properties of multiple LC resonant tanks at different frequencies. A wideband-frequency compensation network is designed to simultaneously utilize the characteristics of LCL low-pass and CLC high-pass circuits within a certain range of frequency variations. Consequently, a unity ratio of the receiver output voltage to the secondary coil open-circuit voltage is achieved, and the receiver reflected impedance to the primary coil is approximately pure-resistive. A full mathematical model of the proposed receiver is derived to explain the principle behind the wideband operation, and a filter approximation-based design method is developed for quick practical implementation. The whole IPT system including the proposed receiver and a typical series-compensated transmitter is modelled to analyze the performance of the power receiver on the system operating frequency variations. A 10W wideband receiver is prototyped and tested within a frequency range of 100kHz to 200kHz, and experimental results show that the output voltage of the proposed receiver is equal to the secondary coil open-circuit voltage, and the reflected impedance to the primary coil is approximately resistive.

articleTitle: Core Loss Separation Method for High Q Inductors
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Power Technology Conference and Expo (WPTCE)
abstract: Magnetic components used in power electronics are typically the largest and least efficient part of the design. For designers of power magnetics it is necessary to have reliable measurements of loss so the appropriate core can be selected. However, this is a challenging task since small errors in phase measurements can cause large errors in core loss. This is particularly challenging for cores with a phase angle close to 90°, i.e. a high Q. In this work a loss separation method and new phase correction method are proposed. Experimental results show the proposed method has lower error than existing state of the art techniques.

articleTitle: Analysis and Design of Domino Inductive Power Transfer System with Improved Quasi-Load-Independent Constant Current Output
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Power Technology Conference and Expo (WPTCE)
abstract: Recent extensive research has focused on frequency regulation in domino inductive power transfer (IPT) systems to achieve quasi-load-independent (QLI) output. However, practical implementation unavoidably leads to output variations due to the existence of the equivalent series resistances (ESRs) of the coils, and investigations into the impact on practical systems are insufficient. To this end, this paper analyzes the characteristics of QLI constant current (CC) output in domino IPT systems considering the ESRs and examines the performance of different CC frequencies in a four-coil domino IPT system.

Author Keywords: quasi load independent constant current (QLI-CC) output

articleTitle: A Low-Power Resonance Detector for Output Power Optimization in Wireless Power Transfer Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Power Technology Conference and Expo (WPTCE)
abstract: This paper introduces a class-D power amplifier (PA) incorporating a power-efficient resonance detection circuit designed for resonant wireless power transfer (WPT) systems. In the operation of resonant WPT systems, the process tolerance of the L-C resonant components on both sides introduce an imaginary part in the equivalent reflected impedance in the PA, resulting in a degradation of the power transferred to the secondary side. The magnitude of the imaginary part can vary depending on the measurement setup of the WPT system, including the coupling distance, misalignment of the coils, and output loading conditions. Therefore, a resonant detector is proposed to estimate the reactance on the primary side and assist in adjusting the magnitude of the compensation capacitance to ensure the resonance of the L-C tank. Additionally, this proposed detector consumes only 249uW during measurement, making it suitable to be employed in low-power applications.

articleTitle: Selective Microwave Wireless Power Beaming for Multiple Devices Using Backscatter CDMA
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Power Technology Conference and Expo (WPTCE)
abstract: Microwave power transmission technology using distributed antenna systems is being researched and developed. The distributed WPT system optimizes the transmission phase and supplies higher power by feeding back fluctuations in received power at receivers to the transmit side. In this study, by using a spread spectrum signal as a backscatter signal, independently receiving feedback signals in the same frequency from multiple receivers, similar to the CDMA system was realized. To implement the CDMA system, we implemented a circuit in the power receiver using a CPLD to generate the Gold sequence, which is a spreading code. On the transmitter side, a demodulator for the superimposed spread spectrum was implemented in the power transmission system using DLL. The proposed WPT system was constructed by integrating the developed power receiving terminal and power transmission system. We confirmed the constructed system can selectively supply power to multiple receivers.

articleTitle: Multi-Object Charging in Room-Sized Weakly Coupled WPT System
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Power Technology Conference and Expo (WPTCE)
abstract: This study introduces a new approach to power management in an inductive one-to-many wireless power transfer (WPT) system. In particular, we provide a theoretical basis for the approach based on circuit theory. The approach shows that in case of negligible direct interaction between receivers, which could be easily achieved in a weak coupling system, no additional components or power tracking is needed if the transmitter provides a stable and uniform magnetic field. In addition, the efficiency of such a system increases with the number of receivers, making it comparable with strong coupling systems despite a weak coupling coefficient. We also propose a practical realization of this approach and confirm our theoretical results by circuit and full wave finite element models. These results lead to a promising future of reliable and affordable weak coupling one-to-many WPT systems.

articleTitle: Recent Advances in Safety Technologies for Wireless Power Transfer Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Power Technology Conference and Expo (WPTCE)
abstract: This paper presents the recent advancements in Wireless Power Transfer (WPT) technology, along with the associated safety issues and solutions. The WPT technology, which transmits power without traditional wires, is being applied in various fields, such as smartphones, medical equipment, and electric vehicles. However, with the proliferation of WPT technology, safety concerns such as exposure to electromagnetic fields, heat generation, and interference between devices have emerged. Therefore, this paper introduces the latest research trends related to the safety of WPT and technological advancements aimed at enhancing safety, and proposes future research directions. This paper provides an understanding of the safety aspects of WPT technology and can be used as a foundational resource for the design and implementation of safe WPT systems.

articleTitle: Calorimetric Measurement of Losses in Nanocrystalline Cores
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Power Technology Conference and Expo (WPTCE)
abstract: Inductive power transfer (IPT) power density requirements have risen in recent years due to increased adoption of electric vehicles (EVs). Nanocrystalline cores have been proposed to improve power density of IPT pads because of their higher saturation limits and Curie temperatures compared to Mn- Zn ferrites. This article demonstrates a method of core-loss measurement that accounts for the anisotropic behaviour of nanocrystalline ribbons using calorimetric methods.

articleTitle: Sensorless Drone Detection for In-Flight Inductive Power Transfer Using Transmitter-Side Voltage Pulses
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Power Technology Conference and Expo (WPTCE)
abstract: In-flight inductive wireless power transfer technique is a solution to extend the flight duration and reduce the battery capacity and charging time for drones. Before the power transmission, the drone detection method on a transmitter side is necessary for the reduction of magnetic field emission and power loss. A sensorless receiver coil detection using transmitter-side voltage pulses has been proposed for electric vehicles (EVs). This paper proposes the sensorless receiver coil detection for drones using the same technique. The main difference between the EVs and drones is the change of the attitude of the receiver coil such as altitude, pitch angle, and roll angle. The threshold of the receiver side current during short mode can be decided based on the coupling coefficient, therefore, the attitude difference does not affect the detection accuracy. The effectiveness of the proposal is experimentally validated using a drone test bench with changes of the altitude and pitch angle.

articleTitle: Optimal Design of a Wireless Power System with the Filter Theory
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Power Technology Conference and Expo (WPTCE)
abstract: Magnetic coupled wireless power transfer (WPT) systems often face challenges in output efficiency degradation due to changes in relative position or load variations. Existing design methods often result in an increase in circuit complexity and an inability to address both distance changes and misalignments simultaneously. In this paper, we present a novel WPT system design method grounded in filter theory. This method treats mutual inductance as a variable corresponding to the frequency parameter in filter design. We then employ the well-established filter design theory to develop multi-coil WPT systems. Using both first-order and second-order Chebyshev filters as the sample, through simulations and experiments, we validate our proposed method and achieve stable transmission efficiency within a specific interval of mutual inductance and load variation.

articleTitle: Design of Wireless Power Transfer System for Low-Speed Vehicles Based on LCC-S Topology
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Power Technology Conference and Expo (WPTCE)
abstract: With the development and application of wireless power transmission (WPT) technology, the value of WPT technology in practical applications is being recognized. According to the actual application requirements of low-speed vehicles and the WPT realization of passenger cars, this paper studies the WPT scheme suitable for low-speed vehicles. For the constant-voltage battery load, a scheme is proposed that the load battery is directly connected to an uncontrolled rectifier and the output power is controlled on the transmitting side through communication. Due to its constant-voltage-output feature, the LCC-S topology is used as the compensation network, which can realize mutual-inductance estimation and auxiliary power supply at the same time. The mutual-inductance estimation formula based on DC voltages is given, which reduces the sampling difficulty and still ensures that the detection accuracy meets the requirement of coil alignment. A 3.3-kW wireless charging prototype was built, the output voltage ranged from 48 to 75V and the max output current reached 60A. The power, efficiency, and mutual-inductance estimation were tested under different coupling and load voltages. The results show that the overall efficiency of the low-voltage large-current system is higher than 85% and the maximum efficiency reaches 88.4%, which verifies the feasibility of the proposed scheme.
