articleTitle: Wireless Power Transfer Model Based Estimation of Rotor Current and Temperature for Inductive Electrically Excited Synchronous Machines
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Power Technology Conference and Expo (WPTCE)
abstract: Inductive wireless power transfer (WPT) system rotor supply for electrically excited synchronous machines enables reduced maintenance requirements and increased power density due to better rotor integration compared to conventional slip rings and brushes. However, the control of the rotor current and monitoring of the rotor winding temperature is challenging as the rotor current and voltage are inaccessible. This paper introduces a rotor estimator based on a semi-analytical steady-state WPT model. The estimation only requires the measurement of the primary side high frequency AC current which is conducted with a FPGA unit. Verification with steady-state and dynamic measurements shows good agreement between measured and estimated current and temperatures and thus, closed-loop current control and temperature monitoring is made possible.

articleTitle: Receiver Capacitor Selection Method for Reducing Leakage Magnetic Field in Double-Sided Wireless Power Transfer System
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Power Technology Conference and Expo (WPTCE)
abstract: In wireless power transfer (WPT) system, some of the magnetic fields generated from the transmitter (TX) are not transferred to the receiver (RX), but leak into the air. In particular, in a double-sided WPT system that can charge two RXs simultaneously with one TX, the leakage magnetic field is increased. There are several methods to reduce the leakage magnetic field, but all of those methods require additional equipment and are focused on the 1 TX-1 RX WPT system. This paper proposes a method to reduce the leakage magnetic field in the double-sided WPT system by adjusting the current phase difference of each coil without using any equipment. In addition, we introduce how to select the optimal RX capacitor to make the phase difference that reduces the leakage magnetic field. By applying the proposed method, the leakage magnetic field can be reduced by up to 43.7 % and at least 11.1 % at the observation point compared to the conventional method.

articleTitle: 900 MHz RF Power Rectifier Based on Ultra-low Turn-on Voltage Quasi-vertical GaN Schottky Diode
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Power Technology Conference and Expo (WPTCE)
abstract: This paper presents a 20 W high-power RF-to-DC rectifier that can be applied to wireless power transfer (WPT) systems. To address the power limitations of conventional diodes, a rectifier is designed based on a gallium nitride (GaN) integrated circuit (IC) quasi-vertical Schottky barrier diode (SBD). Leveraging the advantages of high mobility, wide bandgap, and saturation velocity of the GaN, significant benefits of the diode have been derived, with an ultra-low turn-on voltage of 0.23 ± 0.005 V (at 1 A/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>) and a high breakdown voltage of 180 V, to improve the rectification performance. Using this diode, a high-power rectifier with a wide input power range and high efficiency is developed. The proposed rectifier structure consists of a single-shunt self-developed diode and a topology with class-F harmonics control networks. It achieves a peak power conversion efficiency of 72.9% with an input power of 43 dBm at 900 MHz.

articleTitle: Fault Detection in Series Battery Modules: An Integrated Approach for Micro Short Circuits
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Power Technology Conference and Expo (WPTCE)
abstract: Net-zero carbon emissions are becoming increasingly important, and the rapid development of renewable energy underscores the crucial role of energy storage systems. Among these systems, lithium-ion batteries are the dominant energy storage option. Compared to other types of batteries, lithium-ion batteries exhibit higher charge-discharge efficiency and longer lifespans, providing them with an advantage throughout the entire product lifecycle. As a result, whether it's electric vehicles or energy storage systems, they are typically equipped with lithium-ion battery packs. Battery management systems play a significant role in these lithium-ion battery packs. Improper usage of batteries, such as excessive charge-discharge cycling, can lead to the failure of the insulation layer between electrodes, resulting in micro short circuits within the batteries. When such a phenomenon occurs, the electrolyte often undergoes exothermic reactions, resulting in thermal runaway and threatening user safety.Therefore, this thesis develops an integrated fault detection algorithm for diagnosing micro short circuits in batteries. By integrating five methods, including <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1.</sup>the battery capacity difference detection method based on the open circuit voltage curve fitting, <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2.</sup>the remaining charge capacity detection method, <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3.</sup>the density-based spatial clustering of applications with noise algorithm, <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4.</sup>the standard score algorithm based on the recursive least square algorithm, <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5.</sup>and the mean difference model based on the recursive least square algorithm. A highly accurate fault detection system for lithium-ion batteries has been developed.

articleTitle: On the Control of DC-DC Converters in the SS-Compensated Wireless Power Transfer System
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Power Technology Conference and Expo (WPTCE)
abstract: DC-DC converters are commonly employed in a series-series (SS) compensated wireless power transfer (WPT) receiver for regulating the output voltage. Although DC-DC converters are extremely familiar to the power electronics community, their characteristics become quite different in a WPT receiver system due to its current-source input and the resultant varying input voltage nature. This uniqueness demands further investigation and a more in-depth understanding of DC-DC converters in the WPT system. Such research is important especially when the efficiency and dynamic requirements for the WPT system become higher. This paper focuses on the modeling, stability analysis, and control of DC-DC converters in a SS-compensated WPT receiver. Some interesting findings are presented, and their implications on the parameter and controller design are discussed. The proposed design is well supported with simulation verification.

articleTitle: Research on High Efficiency Ge-Based Schottky Diode for Low-Power Microwave Power Transmission
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Power Technology Conference and Expo (WPTCE)
abstract: Based on the low turn-on voltage of GePb-based semiconductor materials, a Schottky diode for low-power microwave power transmission and energy harvesting is present in this paper, and the conversion efficiency of the rectifying circuit based on the SPICE model of this device is significantly improved under low input power, which will provide technological support for the development of the space solar power station, wireless sensor network and other technologies.

articleTitle: An Investigation on Coil-Splitting Based Multi-Channel Wireless Power Transfer
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Power Technology Conference and Expo (WPTCE)
abstract: This article proposes an input-parallel-output-parallel (IPOP) Series-Series (SS) type circuit topology structure based on a designed splitting coil coupler. By designing several transmission channels, this wireless power transfer (WPT) system has more ability on power transfer with a relatively high efficiency. The theory of enabling balanced transmission of multi-channel is derived, and the inductance relationship expression for balanced transmission of electrical energy is obtained, thus achieving balanced transmission by multi channels. Besides, by designing splitting coils, the anti-offset performance of multi-channel coils is improved. Finally, based on the conclusions obtained above, simulations of balanced transfer and anti-offset performance about design WPT system is conducted. This new design can better enhance anti-offset performance and reduce current stress while maintaining balanced transmission. Finally, theoretical analysis is proved correct through experiments with a output power of 3.3kW, and the efficiency of this prototype can reach 95.7%.

articleTitle: Isolated Single-Input Multiple-Output DC-AC Inverter for Multi-Coil Wireless Power Transfer
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Power Technology Conference and Expo (WPTCE)
abstract: This paper proposes an isolated single-input multiple-output (SIMO) buck-boost DC-AC inverter. It performs a single-stage DC-AC power conversion from a DC input into multiple independent AC outputs. Compared with its counterparts, the proposed inverter achieves a wide range of output voltages. By employing isolation between the input and outputs, this inverter enables high-power wireless power transfer applications without compromising safety and stability. It carries the conspicuous advantages of simple circuit structure, small form factor, and high scalability. The simulation results confirm the feasibility of the isolated single-input three-output (SITO) buck-boost DC-AC inverter topology without cross-regulation.

articleTitle: Electrohydrodynamic Inkjet Printed Flexible Ceramic Rectenna for 5.8 GHz ISM Band
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Power Technology Conference and Expo (WPTCE)
abstract: This work presents the first reported case of a flexible ceramic rectenna operating in the 5.8 GHz ISM band with electrohydrodynamic inkjet (EHDIJ) printed conductors on Corning 40 micron thick alumina ribbon ceramics (ARC). The viability of using EHDIJ as an additive manufacturing method with resolutions of 5µm for integrating bare die integrated circuits (IC) and RF structures such as antennas for wireless power transfer (WPT) is presented. The functional prototype demonstrates WPT at 5.8 GHz in both its rest and flexed state down to a 35 mm bending radius at distances greater than 200 mm with 1W regulatory compliant RF output power and transmit dipole antenna.

articleTitle: Magnetoelectric layers improve spatial variability in wireless power transfer
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Power Technology Conference and Expo (WPTCE)
abstract: Wireless charging is typically based on two well-aligned coils, the emitter and the receiver coil. Distributed coil systems with arbitrarily placed receiving coils suffer from power nulls and need complex control. We demonstrate that it is possible to actively guide and distribute the magnetic field in wireless power transfer (WPT) systems using magnetoelectric (ME) composite materials. Thereby, we enable WPT to also operate with non-aligned coils and enhance positioning freedom. Our research begins with a proof of concept at low frequency, followed by an experimental verification with a WTP system at a resonance frequency of 540 kHz. Finally, we conducted an extensive analysis of our fluxguide by means of simulations.

articleTitle: Experiments on WPT Feedback Control in WPT and Communication System Based on Base Station
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Power Technology Conference and Expo (WPTCE)
abstract: Towards Beyond 5G/6G, factory automation, digital twin, and cyber-physical systems (CPS) are expected to be realized. Internet of Things (IoT) technology for sensing a variety of data in the real world will be necessary to realize these systems. As the number of IoT sensors increases, it becomes a major challenge to deliver power wirelessly to IoT sensors. We propose a communication and Wireless Power Transfer (WPT) system that performs WPT by beamforming from a base station to an IoT sensors in order to supply stable and sufficient power. In previous studies, beam control according to the IoT terminal at the base station is difficult because IoT terminal information is not fed back to the base station. In this study, we develop a communication and WPT system that includes feedback of IoT terminal information to the base station, and demonstrate beam control according to IoT terminal information at the base station.

articleTitle: Enhanced Indoor Light Energy Harvesting Exploiting Over-The-Air Pulse Shaping
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Power Technology Conference and Expo (WPTCE)
abstract: This paper aims to enhance indoor light energy harvesting for Internet of Things (IoT) sensors in the context of simultaneous light and information power transfer (SLIPT). We use the time-delayed optical transmission from multiple sources to construct a near-constant waveform, which we term the waveform shaping method. Thanks to its perfect match with the response of the photovoltaic panel, the energy-converting efficiency can be boosted. We built a complete simulation procedure and real-world testbed to showcase the feasibility of the proposed approach. Simulation and experimental results demonstrate the ability to improve light energy harvesting by up to 24% compared to synchronized optical transmission. These insights pave the way for investigating the trade-offs between data and energy transfer within SLIPT systems.

articleTitle: Basic Study on Transmission Power Enhancement in Dynamic Wireless Power Transfer Systems using Circular–Solenoid Multi-coil
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Power Technology Conference and Expo (WPTCE)
abstract: This paper proposes a method for stable power transmission in dynamic wireless power transfer (DWPT) systems with a coil array installed on the ground. The proposed method adopts a Circular-Solenoid type multi-coil on the electric vehicle (EV) side to utilize both vertical and horizontal magnetic fields, achieving stable power transmission all over the DWPT lane. In the experiments, a prototype was constructed, and the magnetic coupling characteristics of the ground and EV side coils were clarified. The power transmission characteristics were then derived, and a guideline was provided for efficiently and stably transmitting 3 kW of power to EVs all over the DWPT lane.

articleTitle: Cancellation of Magnetic Field Leakage in Fundamental and Harmonic Components for Inductive Power Transfer Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Power Technology Conference and Expo (WPTCE)
abstract: Inductive power transfer (IPT) systems transmit power via magnetic field, therefore electromagnetic compatibility (EMC) and electromagnetic interference (EMI) issues are caused by the magnetic field leakage from the IPT systems. In this study, we propose a method to cancel both the fundamental and harmonic components of the magnetic field leakage in a multiple-input single-output (MISO) system by only controlling the transmitters and the receiver. The fundamental component of the input voltage and the optimum load impedance are derived to maximize power transmission efficiency (PTE) under the cancellation condition of the magnetic field leakage at the fundamental frequency. The harmonic components of the input voltage that can cancel the harmonics of the magnetic field leakage is calculated by estimating the harmonic components generated by the full-bridge rectifier on the receiver side. Circuit simulations were performed to evaluate the proposed method. As a result of the simulations, it was confirmed that the fundamental and harmonic components of the magnetic field leakage can be suppressed by more than 34 dB compared to the PTE maximization method, and that the reduction in PTE was about 1.7 %.

articleTitle: Evaluation of Ferriteless Magnetic Topologies for Dynamic Inductive Power Transfer to Electric Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Power Technology Conference and Expo (WPTCE)
abstract: This paper presents a comparative evaluation of DWPT magnetic topologies aided by design optimisation. With multiple topologies for DWPT magnetics being proposed, it is necessary to identify the best low-cost and compliant designs suitable for public infrastructure. This comparison targets a ferrite-less primary with a power density of 50kW/m. The design objectives are to minimise copper and electronics cost, maximise output power and achieve leakage compliance. For each topology, an NSGA-II optimisation is conducted to select the best design. The magnetic parameters are rapidly resolved with analytical equations for ferrite-less coils, and match closely with ANSYS simulation. Furthermore, the power output is verified by PLECS simulation. The single phase poles across and along the road, and two phase meander track are found to have the best aggregate performance under the selected design criteria. The circular primary is a good low-cost solution, however has a lower average output power than the aforementioned designs. The three-phase with field across the road primary is a promising solution due to low electronics cost, however leakage fields can be an issue. The three-phase with field along the road primary struggled with the high air gap and lack of ferrite leading to low couplings.

articleTitle: Quasioptical Double-Lens 3-m Wireless Power Transfer at 28 GHz With Corrugated Horns
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Power Technology Conference and Expo (WPTCE)
abstract: Having implemented the theory of quasioptics for achieving high beam efficiency in wireless power transfer (WPT) systems, the development of a large-scale demonstrator has been pursued in the context of a solar power satellite system. Here we present a preliminary study aimed at validating different aspects of the radiative subsystem of such demonstrator, including the gaussian beam generation achieved by an additively manufactured corrugated horn, as well as its transformation by a Fresnel lens. Both of these novel solutions have been validated individually and were later used in a double-lens reciprocal system, composing a 3-m WPT experiment, where the maximum beam efficiency of 43% was achieved. These positive results show that the beam propagation aspect of the system is well understood, prompting the implementation of the DC-RF and RF-DC conversion subsystems in order to arrive at the complete WPT system validation. The next step would be the development of the large-scale demonstrator.

articleTitle: A Tunable Active Clamping Source Based High Frequency Single-Switch Resonant Gate Driving Circuit with Duty Cycle and Frequency Modulation Capability
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Power Technology Conference and Expo (WPTCE)
abstract: Resonant Gate Driver (RGD) is an effective method to save gate driver loss at high frequency. Most RGDs require at least two transistors to constitute the bridge structure, which suffers from difficult dead time control at tens of MHz. The single-switch RGDs are easy to implement but can only generate fixed duty cycle waveforms and operate at the narrow band. This paper proposed a single-switch RGD with a wide operation bandwidth, and the duty cycle of output driving voltage can be modulated by easily controlling the tunable active clamping source instead of difficult nanosecond signal control. The experimental results are given to verify the proposed RGD at 12MHz-15MHz with the 1kW Class-E power amplifier

articleTitle: Proposed Method of Embedding Transmission Coils in Reinforced Concrete Pavement with Resin Pavement Material in Dynamic Wireless Power Transfer
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Power Technology Conference and Expo (WPTCE)
abstract: In Dynamic Wireless Power Transfer, the embedment of power transmission coils in the road surface is essential. Previous studies have reported that coil characteristics deteriorate during embedment in reinforced concrete pavement due to the effects of rebar and concrete. In this paper, precast reinforced concrete pavement slabs employing insulated steel bars were used to simulate the embedment of coils in the pavement, and the coil properties due to the embedment were measured. An embedment method using polyurea resin is proposed to reduce the effect of concrete on the coil properties. The results of the embedment simulation test showed that the use of polyurea resin successfully improved the Q-value of the coil by about 85 % compared to the case where concrete was used. Furthermore, the transmission characteristics were evaluated using a vector network analyzer (VNA), and a transmission efficiency of 95.8 % was obtained over a transmission distance of 170 mm.

articleTitle: Theorization of a Compatible Method for Far-field Leakage Magnetic Field Reduction and High Efficiency Power Transfer Using Adjacent Transfer Coil in Dynamic Wireless Power Transfer
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Power Technology Conference and Expo (WPTCE)
abstract: In order to put dynamic wireless power transfer into practical use, it is necessary to reduce the leakage magnetic field, which has adverse effects on the human body and electronic devices, below the regulated value. At the same time, it is necessary to achieve high efficiency power transfer to utilize energy effectively. In this paper, the far-field leakage magnetic field at 10 m from the reference is reduced below the regulated value without adding any devices that are not necessary for power transfer by setting the input voltage to the adjacent transfer coil in the direction of the electric vehicle to be appropriate for the transfer coil that is supplying power. It is shown that the power transfer efficiency, including adjacent transfer coils, can be increased to more than 95 % without any additional equipment that is not required. This method is applicable to the case where S-S, Double-LCC, or LCC-S is used as the resonance method of the circuit, and the leakage magnetic field can be reduced to a maximum of 0.7 mA/m or less with 20 kW of receiving power in any resonance method. The effectiveness of this method is confirmed by theoretical calculations and electromagnetic field analysis using the method of moments.

articleTitle: Wireless Smart Charging Station for Multi-Unmanned Aerial Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Power Technology Conference and Expo (WPTCE)
abstract: Unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) inspection has emerged as a crucial trend in the field of power inspection, owing to its high efficiency and convenience. However, its short cruising range considerably limits the inspection radius. Although wireless power transfer (WPT) technology has made UAV charging more convenient, the conventional "one-to-one" WPT method cannot meet the rapidly changing requirements of the UAV swarm. Therefore, this paper proposes a wireless smart charging station equipped with capacitive power transfer technology, which enables simultaneous wireless charging of multiple UAVs and improves the charging efficiency of UAV swarms. The proposed smart charging station utilizes a bilateral inductor-capacitor (LC) LC compensation topology, where the key is to keep the coupling mechanism port voltage constant regardless of the number of pickups. Moreover, with appropriate parameter design, the multi-pickups are ensured to have a constant current charging independent of load variations. Finally, theoretical analysis and circuit simulation are presented to validate the feasibility and effectiveness of the proposed multi-load wireless smart charging station.

articleTitle: Experimental Validation of the Dynamics of the Both-Sides Retrodirective Antenna Array System
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Power Technology Conference and Expo (WPTCE)
abstract: The retrodirective antenna array is considered as a mechanism to enable target tracking of a power receiver for long range wireless power transfer (WPT) due to its simplicity in implementation using only analog circuits. By installing the retrodirective capability on both the generator and rectenna arrays, a feedback loop that produces a high efficiency WPT channel is created. In this paper, we characterize the dynamics of this phenomenon using a discrete-time state-space model based on S-parameters and show that the system can naturally achieve maximum theoretical WPT efficiency. We further confirmed the theoretical analysis through a hardware experiment using a 12-port circuit board with measurable S-parameters mimicking a static wireless channel. The results collected from the hardware experiment show agreement with the proposed theoretical framework by comparing the theoretical efficiency with the measured efficiency and by showing that the collected data points follow the predicted condition to achieve maximum efficiency.

articleTitle: Single-Core Dual Coils in Wireless Power Transfer Systems with Force-Display Functions
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Power Technology Conference and Expo (WPTCE)
abstract: Conventional wireless power transfer technologies primarily focus on wireless charging devices, overlooking the impact of mechanical connections, such as cable tension on user interfaces. In contrast, we are exploring a wireless power transfer system with force-display functions to enable users to intuitively perceive the power supply status of electronic devices. The system used a permanent magnet on the receiver side and an electromagnet on the transmitter side. The charging status of the electronic device can be intuitively displayed to the user by adjusting the electromagnet based on the circumstances. In this paper, we present the design and implementation of single-core dual coils that realize both electromagnetic and wireless power transfer coils in a single core. Through experimental evaluations, the generation of attractive and repulsive forces up to approximately 2 N was confirmed in terms of the electromagnetic force. In addition, the maximum power transfer efficiency reached 87%.

articleTitle: Mutual Inductance Estimation of SS-IPT Systems with Physics-informed Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Power Technology Conference and Expo (WPTCE)
abstract: Inductive power transfer (IPT) systems heavily rely on accurate values of mutual inductance for efficient and optimal performance. This paper proposes a parameter estimation method for series-series IPT (SS-IPT) systems with a physics-informed neural network (PINN). Firstly, the physics model of SS-IPT systems is established by deducing its ordinary differential equations. Then, the physics model is merged into a neural network to establish PINN. With the PINN, the mutual inductance of the IPT system is identified by using the input current and input voltage of the transmitter-side only. The proposed PINN leverages the power of data-driven technology while incorporating known physics-based principles, leading to more accurate and generalizable identification results. The proposed method is verified in several groups of simulation data. The results show that the estimated error of the proposed method is less than 2% under different coupling coefficients.

articleTitle: Proposition of Novel Evaluation Method and Values for Wireless Power Transfer With Modulated Waves
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Power Technology Conference and Expo (WPTCE)
abstract: Flexible DC power supplying is necessary for the practical use of IoT. There are two main techniques for the power supply. One is the wireless power transfer (WPT) technique and the other is energy harvesting(EH). This paper focuses on WPT with modulated waves and radio-frequency(RF) energy harvesting. Both techniques use rectifiers for the conversion from modulated electromagnetic waves to direct current(DC) power. In recent research, it is revealed that the characteristics of rectifiers with modulated input are calculated with power probability distribution and rectifiers’ own CW characteristics. Herein, we can make the general discussion of the modulated waves for WPT and EH.Previous research show that the modulated waves with high peak-to-average power ratio(PAPR) can improve the RF-DC conversion efficiency of rectifiers when the average input power is low. More strictly speaking, this fact means that the modulation improves the efficiency when the average input power is lower than 1 / PAPR times of the optimum CW input for each rectifier. This is absolutely correct and consistent with much experimental results. However, this is only the sufficient condition and not useful for the practical design. Herein, We focused on the practical and novel evaluation method for the WPT and EH with general modulations. This paper proposes the novel evaluation method for modulations. Our method uses a weighted power probability distribution(PPD). The average and variance of the weighted PPD are practical evaluation parameters for the modulations. The former value approximately equals to the optimum design power for the rectifier with modulated waves and we defined the value as "representative power". The other value can evaluate the modulation quality for WPT. We also show the consistency of these values by comparing with the simulation results.

articleTitle: Improving Metrics for Laser Power Beaming
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Power Technology Conference and Expo (WPTCE)
abstract: Important performance metrics for laser power beaming in three areas are described: efficiency, size- and weight-specific power, and the reaction time plus stand-off distance requirements for active safety sensing. Measurements of these metrics from recent demonstrations are listed. Methods of improvement are outlined, and some future goals are shown.

articleTitle: Gate-folded Triboelectric Energy Harvester for Intelligent Tires
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Power Technology Conference and Expo (WPTCE)
abstract: We have investigated the integration of a triboelectric energy harvester in a tire to provide electrical energy for smart tires. The harvester is made of cost-effective, off-the-shelf materials and is comprehensively characterized in lab environment. Further assessments are conducted within tire test machines, evaluating the harvester’s performance under varying driving conditions. The results points out the potential of this technology in harnessing energy from the tire motion. This energy can be used to power sensor networks, marking a significant step toward sustainable and battery free intelligent tires.

articleTitle: Electric Field Energy Harvesting from High-Voltage Power Lines for Batteryless LoRaWAN
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Power Technology Conference and Expo (WPTCE)
abstract: This work proposes an efficient electric field energy harvester underneath high-voltage power lines for batteryless LoRaWAN communications and sensing applications. Comprehensive theoretical analysis is set to help identify the optimized design (size, separation, and permittivity) of the energy harvester and accurately predict its harvesting performance. A complete batteryless platform has been developed, including an aluminum plates-based harvester, a full bridge rectifier, an ultra-low-power hysteresis comparator, and an Arduino LoRaWAN module. The energy harvester can collect 48-uW power from 525-kV high-voltage power lines. Our preliminary experiments demonstrate that this proposed harvester can successfully drive the LoRaWAN module every 40 minutes for potential kilometers of wireless communications.

articleTitle: Simultaneous Wireless Power and Data Transfer System Based on SP Compensation Topology
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Power Technology Conference and Expo (WPTCE)
abstract: This paper proposes a simultaneous wireless power and data transfer (SWPDT) system. A series-parallel (SP) compensation topology is adopted by considering the energy transfer efficiency and resonant characteristics, which has a constant voltage transfer ratio under resonant frequency via a single inductive coil. Amplitude-shift keying (ASK) modulation technology is employed in data communication, and the encoded data is modulated into a PWM signal. The original encoded data is obtained by demodulating rectified voltage at the receiver. The theoretical analysis preliminarily verified the feasibility of the proposed system, and a prototype was implemented. The transmitter applies GaN to enhance the switching frequency of power switches, and the receiver performs sampling of the demodulated signal. The transmitter and receiver are controlled by DSP and FPGA chips, respectively. Finally, the proposed SWPDT system is demonstrated from the circuit implementation, and the experimental results show the superior performance of simultaneous wireless power and data transfer.

Author Keywords: Simultaneous wireless power and data transfer system

articleTitle: Beyond Rectification: Passive Backscattering Modulation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Power Technology Conference and Expo (WPTCE)
abstract: Wireless Sensor Networks are instrumental to many monitoring systems and control of dynamical systems, allowing real-time and pervasive information collection. However, they are hindered by their dependency on local energy sources, even though their physical transduction principle can be passive. This work proposes an early framework for converting any dc passive sensor into a wireless sensor with passive backscattering modulation capabilities. The operation consists of transforming dc resistance into an RF impedance through the mediation of the nonlinear device of a rectifier.

articleTitle: Analysis of Wind Harvesting and Wireless Power Transfer Integration for Moving Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Power Technology Conference and Expo (WPTCE)
abstract: This paper explores the potential of wind energy harvesting from moving vehicles, focusing on the integration of Wireless Power Transfer (WPT) through inductive charging. The study highlights the urgent need for research in eco-friendly renewable energy systems to address global challenges associated with traditional energy sources. The proposed wind harvester system incorporates a DC motor as energy generator and a power management module, offering a replenishment solution for vehicles. At an average velocity of 80 km/h, it was obtained 3.75 V and a current of 50 mA. Experimental results demonstrate the system’s feasibility and potential for real-world applications, emphasizing its role in reshaping sustainable energy practices.

articleTitle: Computational Study of Microwave Beam Forming for Wireless Power Transfer on Flight-Formation Small-Satellite Experiment
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Power Technology Conference and Expo (WPTCE)
abstract: In this study, array scheme and inter-satellite distance (sat-distance) that maximize efficiency were considered. Space solar power (SSP), wherein solar panels are positioned in space to generate electricity and transmit it to the ground via microwaves, attracts attention. European Space Agency (ESA) is planning a demonstration experiment of wireless power transfer using flight-formation small satellites, whose transmitting antennas are replaced with a large aperture antenna. Four cases are considered: a) the ideal case, b) the case of a single satellite failure, c) the case of a deviation in satellite positions, and d) the case of deviation in phase of satellites’ electric field. In the case of a) and b), the triangular array is more efficient. In the case of c), square array is partly more efficient. In the case of d), efficiencies decrease significantly as the deviation increases.

articleTitle: Dynamic Wi-Fi Channel Switching Based On Frequency Characteristics For Wireless Power Transfer
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Power Technology Conference and Expo (WPTCE)
abstract: Numerous IoT sensors will be required in the pursuit of a smart society. As these sensors will be installed in various places, a wireless power supply is essential. Wireless power transfer utilizing communication radio waves has attracted interest as a potential solution, but since the power of a communication radio wave is relatively small, the generated power needs to be increased before we can expand the usage of wireless power transfer. While there has been extensive research on ways of controlling the radio transmission time and improving the efficiency of the radio frequency-direct current converter, control of the communication radio frequency has rarely been studied. In this work, we investigate how the generated power can be improved by controlling the communication radio frequency. The results demonstrate that it is possible to achieve a more efficient wireless power transfer system by selecting the appropriate frequency. Our findings will enable the expansion of use cases—for example, an acceleration sensor and a blood pressure sensor can be run using a single universal software radio peripheral.

articleTitle: 10 kW Small-Gap Wireless Power Transfer System with Asymmetric Pads for Electric Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Power Technology Conference and Expo (WPTCE)
abstract: In wireless power transfer systems for electric vehicles, the volume, cost, and complexity of the system increase due to the consideration of a large air gap and misalignment between the transmitter pad and the receiver pad. This paper proposes a small-gap wireless power transfer system with asymmetric pads to increase the misalignment tolerance and enhance the performance of the wireless power transfer system. The proposed system reduces the air gap to a practical limit using a simple z-axis actuator while the x-axis is aligned by a mechanical stopper. The remaining y-axis misalignment is resolved with the asymmetric structure of the proposed pad. The proposed asymmetric pad enables the wireless power transfer system to maintain consistent performance under considerable y-axis misalignment. The experimental verification of the proposed asymmetric pad is conducted with a 10 kW system prototype. The maximum efficiency of 95.1 % was achieved under a negligible y-axis misalignment, and a 94.0 % efficiency was obtained with the maximum y-axis misalignment of 100 mm.

articleTitle: Millimeter Wave Dual-Polarized Semi-Passive Energy Detection Backscattering RFID
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Power Technology Conference and Expo (WPTCE)
abstract: This paper presents a dual-polarized semi-passive energy detection backscattering RFID at 28 GHz. A 2 by 2 dual-polarized patch antenna array, a Wilkinson power combiner, a low noise FET switch, and a half-wave self-biased rectifier made of a MA4E2037 Schottky diode are designed and optimized on Rogers RO4350B substrate. The antenna is dual-polarized to separate energy harvesting/detection and backscattering features of the system. By adding the biasing load, the rectifier has a low turn-on input power level and can output 0.3 V at an input power of −5 dBm. It reaches the highest power conversion efficiency of 40.2 % with an input power of 12.2 dBm. The rectifier provides a low voltage into a low-power op-amp that connects to an oscillator feeding into a low-noise FET switch for backscattering signal modulation at 270 kHz. This RFID tag can operate up to 40 m with 75 dBm EIRP.

articleTitle: Robust Communicationless Control Strategy to Synchronize In-Motion Secondary to the Primary
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Power Technology Conference and Expo (WPTCE)
abstract: Dynamic wireless power transfer (DWPT) systems for electric vehicles can benefit significantly from the use of secondary active rectifiers by adding useful features such as bi-directional power flow, output power regulation, active control of the reflected impedance, and simplified vehicle detection. This has introduced the need for robust and reliable controls to mitigate some of the key dynamic challenges. A control scheme is proposed in this paper that uses zero crossing detection (ZCD) of free resonant current to synchronize the in motion secondary inverter to the primary inverter. The presented approach is capable to compensate for the detuning of the WPT system through rectifier impedance regulation which also results in efficiency optimization. A discrete time phase locked loop (PLL) synchronization controller comprising of a stabilizing PI compensator is designed and analyzed. The design is validated through simulations and experimental results from a 10 kW prototype system are presented.

articleTitle: Temperature-Dependent Performance of Acoustic Power Transfer Through Metal
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Power Technology Conference and Expo (WPTCE)
abstract: We analyze the effect of temperature on piezoelectric 1-3 composite transducers and their performance in acoustic power transfer through metal at elevated temperatures. Using the resonance analysis in thickness extension mode, we determined temperature-dependent piezoelectric, elastic, and dielectric material coefficients, along with the corresponding electromechanical coupling factor. The dielectric coefficient increased with temperature, while the elastic stiffness and the piezoelectric coefficient decreased with a rise in temperature. Further, we observed thermal hysteresis in all the material parameters over temperature cycles.Subsequently, we investigated the suitability of 1-3 composite piezoelectric transducers for acoustic power transfer at elevated temperatures. Our power transfer system used a 20 mm thick Aluminium wall as a transmitting medium and a pair of transducers glued coaxially to either side for generating and receiving acoustic waves. Results indicate that the efficiency of the acoustic power transfer system is strongly temperature-dependent, exhibiting a decrease with rising temperatures.

articleTitle: Multiple Folding Coils Design for Octagonal Prism-Based Wireless Charging Container with Even Magnetic Flux Density Distribution
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Power Technology Conference and Expo (WPTCE)
abstract: This paper presents an octagonal prism-based wireless charging container with multiple folding coils winding equidistantly around the surface of the container. The optimal coefficient for the equant ratio has been identified to be 1/7 for achieving a more even distribution of magnetic flux compared to the conventional design of the octagonal prism-based wireless charging container. This advancement enables omnidirectional wireless charging for multiple dynamic receivers with minimal power fluctuations.

articleTitle: DisCoBeam for Future WPT Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Power Technology Conference and Expo (WPTCE)
abstract: This paper presents an advanced Distributed Coherent Beamforming (DisCoBeam) concept that can potentially be used to enable a low-cost space-based wireless power transmission (WPT) solution. The proposed concept uses a proliferated low Earth orbit (pLEO) CubeSat constellation. The constellation consists of N number of low size, weight, power, and cost (SWaP-C) satellites. The DisCoBeam concept requires each satellite to be equipped with solar power collecting arrays, a microwave transmitting antenna, and a GPS receiver for accurate position, navigation, and timing (PNT). This allows the satellites to work together to form a coherent microwave beam on a targeted ground rectenna receiver (RX) . Under ideal operational conditions, it will be shown that the proposed DisCoBeam concept can enhance the space-based WPT efficiency by a factor of N-squared. Leveraging the dynamic systems-of-systems (SoS) MATLAB simulator developed by CSUF team for unmanned aerial system (UAS) platforms, we show that the proposed DisCoBeam can achieve about 72% of N-squared at the maximum slant range assuming the PNT of each UAS platform are known precisely and the flight-path strategy results in a linear uniformly-distributed beamforming array within a 1-mile square area with a maximum number of 10 UAS platforms. Finally, the paper discusses the extension of the UAS results to the proposed pLEO satellites scenario.

articleTitle: Wireless Electric Road Systems – Technology Readiness and Recent Developments
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Power Technology Conference and Expo (WPTCE)
abstract: The progress in dynamic wireless power transfer (D-WPT) led to the availability of wireless Electric Road Systems (wERS) that offer smart infrastructure solutions that can substantially reduce transport emissions and electric vehicle (EV) range anxiety. The basis of this technology is resonant Wireless Power Transfer (WPT), which was first demonstrated in the 1890s by Nikola Tesla and has since been developed for various applications. This paper illustrates the state of Electreon’s wERS technology by insights from current pilot projects as well as progress from active R&D activities.

articleTitle: NSGA-II Based Optimization of PCB Coil Array for Inductive Power Transfer
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Power Technology Conference and Expo (WPTCE)
abstract: Inductive power transfer (IPT) systems are used in a wide range of applications. However, their practicality is reduced by the requirement of good alignment between the transmitter and receiver. One way to improve the misalignment tolerance is to use coil arrays. This paper presents an optimization of PCB coil array for charging of a single coil receiver, both with ferrite. The optimization goal is to maximize the average efficiency while minimizing the coil array size and maintaining at least 15 W of transferred power at any position in the working area. Three array types are evaluated, all of which are based on a three-layer hexagonal pattern to provide homogenous magnetic field. Optimization employs the genetic algorithm NSGA-II with magnetic parameters for the coil array geometry evaluated using Maxwell Ansys. The optimized array operates with average efficiency of 84.4 % across all evaluated alignment positions.

articleTitle: A Novel Architecture of Retro-reflective Beamforming for Wireless Power Transmission
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Power Technology Conference and Expo (WPTCE)
abstract: A novel architecture of retro-reflective beamforming is proposed for wireless power transmission applications. In contrast to the conventional architecture with a two-dimensional wireless power transmitting antenna array controlled by a two-dimensional pilot signal receiving antenna array, the novel architecture includes a two-dimensional wireless power transmitting antenna array controlled by multiple one-dimensional pilot signal receiving antenna arrays. The architecture proposed in this paper has better flexibility and lower cost than conventional schemes of retro-reflective beamforming. Theoretical analysis indicates that the novel architecture has similar performance compared with the conventional architecture when the location of a wireless power receiver with a clear line-of-sight path is not far off the broadside direction of the retro-reflective beamformer.

articleTitle: Development of WPT Systems for Railway Vehicles and Study for Low-Frequency Application
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Power Technology Conference and Expo (WPTCE)
abstract: We designed the WPT system for railway vehicles that has a maximum transfer power capacity of approximately 1 MW per car. This system is of the magnetic field coupling type, in which a figure-eight-shaped coils are energized with a high frequency of approximately 10 kHz. Validation through bench tests using a scaled-down experimental device confirms the design’s efficacy. Despite the advantages, high-frequency systems exhibit drawbacks such as large AC losses and high equipment costs. We explored frequency reduction possibilities, particularly aiming at commercial frequencies, anticipating significant cost reductions by omitting a high-frequency inverter on the ground. An example at 50 Hz shown the feasibility of 300 kW power transfer per car while maintaining coil spacing. Modifying the ground coil structure by adding an iron core improved magnetic coupling, suppressing onboard circuit capacity increase, and allowing for equipment dimensions suitable for onboard mounting.

articleTitle: Coupling-Based Multi-Objective Optimization of a Flush Ground Primary Coil for WPT3 SAE J2954 Vehicle Assemblies
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Power Technology Conference and Expo (WPTCE)
abstract: This paper presents a design proposal of flush ground primary transfer coils that achieve optimal inductive coupling with the WPT3 vehicle assemblies of the light-duty SAE J2954, taking coil misalignment into account. For this purpose, a 3D FEA multi-objective optimization was performed accross the design space of the coil geometry parameters. By properly reducing the number of design variables and boundary conditions, the numerical efficiency could be significantly increased and an approximation for the pareto-optimal scaling of the primary coil size could be derived. It is found that at worst coil alignment, the maximum achievable coupling factor of a flush ground primary coil with Z1, Z2 and Z3 secondary side is around 0.07. A comparison to ideal coil alignment as well as a magnetic stray field evaluation concludes the paper.

articleTitle: Wireless Power Supply for Driving UV Lamps based on Autonomous Push-pull Converter with Additional Bias Network
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Power Technology Conference and Expo (WPTCE)
abstract: This paper aims to develop a wireless/contactless power supply to drive an ultraviolet (UV) lamp by designing an MHz autonomous push-pull inverter with an additional bias network. The phase-splitting inductors of the inverter are coupled with receiver coils to reduce the total size and weight of the power supply. A bias network is introduced to the primary resonant tank to hold the operating frequency of the push-pull inverter. The frequency bifurcation range is narrowed for obtaining a high voltage gain to ignite the UV lamp. Theoretical analyses were performed based on a simplified equivalent circuit model to identify the three bifurcation frequencies of the system. In-depth analyses were conducted to evaluate the effect of the bias network on both the frequency bifurcation range and the voltage gain of the system. An equation was derived to determine the optimal value of the secondary tuning capacitor for maximizing the system’s voltage gain under bifurcated conditions. The proposed system and theoretical analysis are validated by simulation study first, then a prototype with a DC input voltage of 16 V and a nominal frequency of 1 MHz is built. It is demonstrated that the actual striking voltage can reach 290 V, which is sufficiently high to ignite the UV lamp for a successful transition to steady-state operation.
